| ID | Rule |
|---|---|
| OLC-01 [7I] | **`organizations.status` is a protected lifecycle column.** It is written by no login role directly, on insert only as `ACTIVE`, and afterwards only inside one of the four lifecycle functions of OLC-05. The single other writer is the restore-only function of OEA-16, which exists only during a restore quarantine and can set only `CANCELLED`. |
| OLC-02 [OD-7I-21, condition 13] | **Grants.** `REVOKE INSERT, UPDATE ON organization.organizations FROM app_api, app_worker`. `app_api` receives column-level `INSERT` on the creation columns and column-level `UPDATE` on the tenant-configuration columns, `logo_storage_ref`, `owner_user_id` and `updated_at`, exactly as the inventory above states, and on no other column. `app_worker` and the nine context principals keep `SELECT` only. `app_platform_admin` keeps `SELECT` only (`105_5B4`, unchanged). A column-level `REVOKE` under the table-level grant would do nothing (the PAS-02 mechanism; §8.6). This refines STP-02 for this relation: the column set is the one stated here, and it excludes `status`. |
| OLC-03 [7I] | **Creation.** 6C-001 inserts the organization with `status = 'ACTIVE'` and then the owner membership (6C §7.7). That stays a direct `INSERT` by `app_api`. A row-level `BEFORE INSERT` trigger rejects a row whose `status` is not `ACTIVE` unless `current_user` is the function-owner role (the STP-03 form: no flag, no session setting). Membership initialization is untouched: `organization.memberships` keeps its grants and its forced RLS. |
| OLC-04 [OD-7I-21, conditions 10, 11] | **Transition trigger.** A row-level `BEFORE UPDATE` trigger fires when `status` changes and enforces three things. (a) An `OLD.status` of `CANCELLED` raises for **every** caller, the function-owner role included: `CANCELLED` is terminal (6C §7.1; `105_5B4`). (b) The edge must be one of the four of OLC-05. (c) `current_user` must be the function-owner role, which a direct caller can never be, because no login role is a member of it. The trigger reads no session setting and takes no argument (PRV-18). It is defence in depth behind the column privilege and it also binds every present and future definer function to the legal edges. |
| OLC-05 [FROZEN + OD-7I-21] | **Every edge has one function and one named authority.** See the table below. The matrix restates frozen 6C §7.1 and 6M §16. It adds no state, no edge and no route. There is no tenant reactivation (6C §7.4, DEP-6C-01) and no platform cancellation (no frozen function or route defines one); neither is introduced. |
| OLC-06 [7I] | **Tenant edges are `API` edges of STP-06.** `ACTIVE → SUSPENDED` (6C-006) and `ACTIVE or SUSPENDED → CANCELLED` (6C-007) run inside two Organization-owned functions executable by `app_api` only, each checking `session_user`. Each requires an API action proof (STP-06) whose bound permission is `organization:suspend` or `organization:delete` respectively, whose organization equals the argument, and whose request identifier is unused. Each carries the frozen compare-and-swap statement of 6C §7.6 unchanged, writes the frozen audit row (`ORGANIZATION_SUSPENDED`, `ORGANIZATION_CANCELLED`) through `audit.fn_insert_audit_event` and a provenance row (STP-11) in the same transaction, and returns "0 rows" as the frozen `409 STATE_CONFLICT`. `confirm_slug` stays a request validation. A holder of the `app_api` password who cannot mint the proof is refused before any row is touched. |
| OLC-07 [OD-7I-21, conditions 3, 4, 5] | **Platform action proof.** A keyed digest, under the **platform action key**, over a length-prefixed encoding of: the purpose label; a unique proof identifier; the authenticated administrator's user identifier; that administrator's session identifier; `organization_id`; the action code (`PLATFORM_SUSPEND` or `PLATFORM_REACTIVATE`); the issue time and the expiry. The lifetime is short ([REC] at most 60 seconds). It is minted by the **platform authorization issuer**, the platform's central internal token issuer (6B §17; the OPA-09 precedent), only after 6B authentication and platform-admin authorization have succeeded for that request and that session. The platform action key is a third key in the protected relation of STP-10, with the same versioning, loading and rotation rules. It is distinct from the API action key and the delivery key, and it is not derivable from, stored with, or retrievable by means of the `app_platform_admin` database credential. |
| OLC-08 [OD-7I-21, conditions 6, 12] | **Verification inside the function.** The superseding platform functions keep the frozen `is_platform_admin()` check and add, before any row is locked: the code verifies under a current or previous key version (`pgcrypto`); the proof's action code equals the function's own constant; its `organization_id` and administrator identifier equal the arguments; the expiry is in the future on the database clock; the bound session exists in `identity.sessions` for that user with `status = 'ACTIVE'`, no `revoked_at` and an unexpired `expires_at`; the bound user's `status` is `ACTIVE`. The session setting `app.is_platform_admin`, the argument `p_admin_user_id` and every other argument are compared with the proof; none of them is evidence by itself. The platform-admin role itself is a 6B claim with no database column, so its revocation reaches the function through the session revocation 6B performs and, at the latest, through the proof's expiry. |
| OLC-09 [OD-7I-21, conditions 7, 8, 9] | **Single use, consumed with the transition.** The proof identifier is inserted into an insert-only consumed-proof relation, under a unique constraint, in the same transaction as the transition and its audit row. A second presentation fails on the constraint and the function raises with nothing changed. A suspension proof cannot reactivate (action code), cannot act on another organization (bound organization), cannot be used from another session or for another administrator (bound identifiers), cannot be used after expiry, and cannot be used after the session is revoked (OLC-08). No runtime role has a table privilege on the consumed-proof relation. |
| OLC-10 [FROZEN; OD-7I-21, conditions 1, 2, 10] | **Preserved.** The 6M routes `POST /platform-admin/organizations/{id}/suspend` and `…/reactivate` and their request and response shapes; 6B authentication and platform-admin authorization; the reason bound of 10 – 2,000 characters; `SELECT … FOR UPDATE` on the organization row; the idempotent no-op on an unchanged target state; the refusal on `CANCELLED`; the same-transaction audit rows `ORGANIZATION_SUSPENDED` and `ORGANIZATION_REACTIVATED` with `previous_status` and `reason` (`107_5B5`). Statements are carried over one for one. 7B lists `organization.suspended` (DS-02) and `organization.cancelled` (DS-03) for the tenant routes with no current consumer and catalogues no platform-route lifecycle event; this section adds, removes and renames none, and any outbox row a frozen contract binds to an edge is inserted in the function's transaction (7F TXA-01). |
| OLC-11 [7I] | **Superseding ACLs (PRV-28).** The proof is an additional argument, so the superseding platform functions are new signatures. The frozen three-argument signatures stay in place, unedited, with `EXECUTE` revoked from `app_platform_admin`, from every other role and from `PUBLIC`: left executable, they would be the bypass. The new signatures are executable by `app_platform_admin` only. The two tenant functions are executable by `app_api` only. The migration ends with an assertion block: for the governed list of functions whose bodies write `organizations.status`, each ACL equals its target set; `has_column_privilege(role, …, 'status', 'UPDATE')` and table-level `UPDATE` are false for every login role; `pg_auth_members` has no row involving the function-owner role. |
| OLC-12 [7I] | **Definer functions and inherited privileges cannot reopen it.** Today two function names write the row and both are superseded (OLC-11). The roles are flat and nothing is granted to `PUBLIC` (§8.5). A later migration that adds a function writing `status` is caught twice: its statement must pass the transition trigger (OLC-04), so it cannot leave `CANCELLED` or invent an edge, and the assertion block of OLC-11 fails the migration unless the function is in the governed list with its target ACL. `BYPASSRLS` is irrelevant here: the table has no RLS, and column and function ACLs are not row policies. |
| OLC-13 [FROZEN] | **Lock order and the 7H admission guarantees.** Each lifecycle function takes the organization row's exclusive lock (the frozen `FOR UPDATE`, or the row lock of the compare-and-swap `UPDATE`) and no delivery, endpoint or anchor lock, exactly as 7H ADM-04 assumes of "the status-changing functions". The proof verification and the session read happen before that lock; the consumed-proof insert, the audit insert and the provenance insert happen after it and take no lock that an admission, a claim or a sweep waits for. 7H ADM-01 … ADM-07 and G1 … G5 are unchanged. |
| OLC-14 [OD-7I-21, condition 14] | **Crash, retry, concurrency.** A function is one transaction: transition, audit, provenance and proof consumption commit together or not at all. A crash before commit leaves the status unchanged and the proof unconsumed; it expires. A crash after commit and before the response: the caller retries, the issuer mints a new proof, the function finds the target state and returns the frozen idempotent result. Two concurrent requests with distinct proofs serialize on the row lock; the second finds the state and is a no-op. Two presentations of one proof: one consumes it, the other fails on the unique constraint. A tenant cancel racing a platform reactivation serializes on the row; whichever commits second re-reads the state under its lock, and a reactivation that finds `CANCELLED` raises. |
| OLC-15 [7I] | **Refusals.** A direct `UPDATE` of `status` fails with `42501` before any row is locked. A function call with a missing, wrong, expired, consumed, cross-organization, cross-action or cross-session proof raises before the organization row is locked, changes nothing and consumes nothing. A legal call on an illegal edge raises from the function (frozen messages) or from the trigger. Each refusal is a security signal (HE-7J-7I-12); no control in this section relies on the signal. |
| OLC-16 [OD-7I-21] | **What is and is not claimed.** *Prevented:* a stolen `app_api`, `app_worker` or context-principal password changing any organization's status by SQL or by a function call; a stolen `app_platform_admin` password doing so, because it cannot compute a proof; reactivation of a `CANCELLED` organization by any runtime path. *Not prevented, and not claimed:* a compromised platform authorization issuer, or a reader of the key relation (migration role, superuser, backup), can mint; a compromised API process can authorize the two tenant edges, as STP-16 already states for `API` edges. Those are RR-09 and RR-08. *Outside this section:* `owner_user_id` and the membership rows remain writable under a stolen `app_api` credential by the frozen tenancy model (RR-01); that is recorded for 7L (HE-7L-7I-10) and is not a lifecycle-status path. |

**The edge matrix (OLC-05).**

| Edge | Function | Executable by | Authority verified in the database | Frozen source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| (insert) → `ACTIVE` | Direct `INSERT`, confined by OLC-03 | `app_api` | None beyond authentication: creation precedes any tenant context (6C §15.1) | 6C §7.7 |
| `ACTIVE → SUSPENDED` | Tenant suspend function | `app_api` | API action proof for `organization:suspend` (OLC-06) | 6C §15.6 |
| `ACTIVE → CANCELLED`, `SUSPENDED → CANCELLED` | Tenant cancel function | `app_api` | API action proof for `organization:delete` (OLC-06) | 6C §15.7 |
| `ACTIVE → SUSPENDED` | Superseding platform suspend | `app_platform_admin` | Platform action proof `PLATFORM_SUSPEND` (OLC-07 … OLC-09) | 6M §16; `107_5B5` |
| `SUSPENDED → ACTIVE` | Superseding platform reactivate | `app_platform_admin` | Platform action proof `PLATFORM_REACTIVATE` | 6M §16; `107_5B5` |
| `CANCELLED →` anything | **None** | — | Not expressible (OLC-04 a) | 6C §7.1 |

**Suspension racing a webhook admission.** Let S be a platform suspension and P a 7H admission (T-04a) for the same organization. P holds or requests `FOR SHARE` on the organization row; S requests `FOR UPDATE`. These conflict. Either P's transaction commits first, releasing its lock, and S commits after it, so the request P admitted falls under 7H's stated 6-second residual (ADM-05 G3, ADM-06); or S holds the row first, P waits, and on obtaining the row PostgreSQL re-evaluates it at its latest committed version in `READ COMMITTED`, P sees `SUSPENDED` and executes T-09 (7H ADM-02). There is no interleaving in which P reads `ACTIVE`, S commits and P then commits an admission. The dispatch claim uses `FOR SHARE SKIP LOCKED` and skips the organization for that poll (ADM-03). This is the frozen argument; what this section adds is that the **only** transactions able to be S are the four lifecycle functions, each carrying a verified authority, so the status P reads under its lock is an authorized status.

**The counterexample, closed.** With IR-45 applied: `UPDATE organization.organizations SET status = 'ACTIVE' WHERE id = …` under `app_api` or `app_worker`, with any tenant setting, fails with `42501 permission denied for table organizations`, because neither role holds table-level `UPDATE` or a column privilege on `status`. The same holder calls the tenant suspend or cancel function: without a proof it cannot compute, the function raises. It cannot call the platform functions at all (`42501`; `107_5B5`). A holder of the `app_platform_admin` password calls the superseding reactivate function with an invented proof: the code does not verify and the function raises; it calls the frozen three-argument signature: `42501`. The organization stays `SUSPENDED`, the admission executes T-09 and the delivery stays held. Until IR-45 exists every one of these statements succeeds, and AB-7I-01 therefore blocks the dispatcher. Tests: VT-96 … VT-100.

### 8.11 Contractual residency fields (P1-7I-R13, residency part; OD-7I-22)

Nothing in this section exists. It is a requirement on a future governed migration (IR-46) with a controlled erratum to 5B, 4I and 6C (ERR-7I-20, ERR-7I-23).

**Amended by OD-7I-25 (P1-7I-R16).** The third remediation let a governed change assign `INDIA_ENTERPRISE` to an existing organization after checking, under the organization's row lock, that it held no data. That check does not hold. Across migrations `001` – `112` exactly five relations have a foreign key to `organization.organizations` (`memberships`, `teams`, `team_memberships` in `003_5B`; `compliance_policies`, `data_subject_requests` in `004_5B`). Every other tenant relation, `webhooks.webhook_endpoints` (`062_5I` L3 – L27) and `audit.domain_event_outbox` (`077_5J1`) among them, takes no lock on the organization row when a row is inserted. In `READ COMMITTED` the interleaving the fourth review gives is therefore real: the change reads an empty inventory; a tenant request inserts an endpoint and commits without ever waiting on the organization row; the change commits the profile. The organization would be certified as data-free when it was not. **The check-then-assign design is withdrawn.** In V1 an organization is `INDIA_ENTERPRISE` from its first committed state or never (CRF-04, CRF-13): no existing organization is converted, so there is no inventory to check and nothing to race.

**Physical and frozen facts.** `data_residency_profile` (`STANDARD` default, `INDIA_ENTERPRISE`, `REGIONAL`) and `region_ref` (`standard` default) are columns of `organization.organizations` (`003_5B` L29 – L30, L45). They are covered by the table-level `INSERT, UPDATE` of `003_5B` L54 and by nothing else: no trigger, no function, no RLS. 6C §7.2 excludes both from `PATCH` as "contractual, not self-service — no permission exists for it either"; the creation request of 6C §15.1 does not carry them, so a new organization takes the defaults; 6M defines no route or function for them; 5B §26 pairs `STANDARD` with `standard`, `INDIA_ENTERPRISE` with `in-primary` and marks `REGIONAL` "Future; per contract". **No frozen source defines an authorized writer.** Today the only way to make an organization `INDIA_ENTERPRISE` is a direct SQL statement, and the same statement by a stolen `app_api` or `app_worker` credential makes any organization `STANDARD`.

**Why it matters to this document.** EGR-01 reads the profile: a `STANDARD` organization has tenant-directed egress by default; an `INDIA_ENTERPRISE` organization has none without a platform-set permission. A silent downgrade therefore removes the egress restriction of OD-7I-04 without touching the egress policy store, and INV-14 and Matrix 10 are evaluated against a profile an attacker chose.

| ID | Rule |
|---|---|
| CRF-01 [OD-7I-22] | **Protected contractual fields.** `organization.organizations.data_residency_profile` and `organization.organizations.region_ref`. They form a third inventory, distinct from the guard columns of STP-01 and from the lifecycle column of OLC-01: they are not written by any tenant action, any platform-administrator action, any event handler or any runtime workload. |
| CRF-02 [OD-7I-22, conditions 1, 3] | **No runtime privilege.** No login role holds `INSERT` or `UPDATE` on either column: the column grants of OLC-02 exclude both for `app_api`; `app_worker`, the context principals and `app_platform_admin` hold no write privilege on the table at all. A tenant `OWNER` or `ADMIN`, an API key and an ordinary platform-administrator connection therefore have no path, because each of them ends in one of those roles. |
| CRF-03 [OD-7I-22, conditions 1, 2] | **Creation takes the frozen default.** Because `app_api` has no column-level `INSERT` on either column, a creating statement cannot name them and the column defaults apply: `STANDARD` and `standard`, as 6C §15.1 and 5B §24 produce today. The `BEFORE INSERT` trigger of OLC-03 additionally rejects any row whose pair is not (`STANDARD`, `standard`) unless `current_user` is the function-owner role. |
| CRF-04 [OD-7I-22, condition 10; OD-7I-25, conditions 7, 9] | **No update, by anyone, in V1.** A row-level `BEFORE UPDATE` trigger raises whenever either column would change, for **every** caller, the function-owner role included. There is no authorization that makes an update pass and no state in which one is permitted. The two values of a row are therefore the values of its first committed state for as long as the row exists. The trigger reads no session setting and trusts no argument; it applies inside every `SECURITY DEFINER` function, present or future, so a definer function cannot be the bypass. |
| CRF-05 [OD-7I-22, conditions 4, 12; OD-7I-25, conditions 1, 5, 12] | **Provisioning authority.** An `INDIA_ENTERPRISE` organization is created only by a governed, owner-approved provisioning change performed outside normal runtime, under the migration authority (PRV-15), which D0 refuses as a runtime identity (INV-03). The change inserts a **provisioning authorization** and calls the provisioning creation function of CRF-13, on which **no login role that any runtime workload uses holds `EXECUTE`**: not `app_api`, `app_worker`, a context principal, `app_platform_admin` or any narrow principal. The authorization relation carries no privilege for any login role. The authorization records, before the organization exists: the contract reference; the change-record reference; two distinct human identities, proposer and reviewer; the contracted region; the deployment-conformance evidence reference of CRF-06; the intended owner's user identifier; the organization's creation attributes (name, slug, country, currency); times. It is not an API, not a 6M route and not a tooling capability, and no tenant administrator, API key or platform-administrator session can reach it. |
| CRF-06 [OD-7I-22, conditions 5, 6, 9; OD-7I-25, conditions 1, 10, 11, 12] | **Preconditions checked inside the creation function, before it inserts anything.** (a) The only pair it can create is (`INDIA_ENTERPRISE`, `in-primary`); `REGIONAL` stays "Future" as 5B §26 has it. (b) The authorization is `APPROVED`, unconsumed, names two different humans, and is locked for the transaction. (c) **Deployment conformance, fail closed:** the database carries a governed deployment-region record stating that this deployment is the contracted region and that every store of Matrix 10 (RSY-01 … RSY-13) passed its conformance check; the function raises if the record is absent, stale, or names a region other than the one in the authorization. A tenant therefore cannot be created as `INDIA_ENTERPRISE` in a deployment that does not satisfy the requirement, and a mismatch between contract and environment creates nothing. (d) **The owner:** the named user exists in `identity.users` with `status = 'ACTIVE'`; the function raises otherwise. (e) **Before tenant data processing, by construction:** the organization does not exist until this transaction commits, and its identifier is generated inside the function. As a defence against a planted row, the function also asserts that no relation of the governed data-bearing inventory holds a row with that identifier. (f) No egress permission of EGR-01 is created, so the organization starts with no outbound webhook or plugin egress, as OD-7I-04 requires. |
| CRF-07 [OD-7I-22, conditions 7, 8, 13, 14; OD-7I-25, conditions 7, 8, 9] | **No conversion, no relocation, no downgrade, no runtime upgrade.** An existing organization's profile never changes in V1: the creation function takes no organization identifier and has no path for an existing row, and the trigger of CRF-04 refuses every update. An organization that signed up as `STANDARD` and later contracts for enterprise residency is given a new organization by provisioning; its existing data is not relabelled. Relocating existing data to or from a region is a separate approved process covering the databases, recordings, object storage, Redis, backups, audit, recovery material, secrets and external transfer policy; none is designed here. No online residency-upgrade API, route or function exists. A tighten-only or bidirectional capability is a future governed owner decision. Ordinary self-service creation keeps the frozen `STANDARD` default (CRF-03). |
| CRF-08 [7I; OD-7I-25, condition 5] | **Forged context and indirect paths.** `app.tenant_id` and `app.is_platform_admin` are irrelevant: no rule above reads either. No definer function writes these columns today (§8.10 table); the trigger of CRF-04 refuses any update by any function; and an insert of a non-default pair passes the insert trigger of CRF-03 only when `current_user` is the function-owner role, which holds for exactly one function, the creation function, whose ACL is empty of runtime roles. The roles are flat; nothing is granted to `PUBLIC`; no default privilege exists (§8.5). The assertion block of IR-46 checks `has_column_privilege` for both columns and both privileges over every login role, `has_function_privilege` false for every login role on the creation function, and that the governed list of functions able to insert an organization row equals that one function. |
| CRF-09 [FROZEN; OD-7I-22, condition 11] | **Ordinary profile updates are preserved.** The `PATCH` of 6C-003 writes only the columns of 6C §7.2, each of which `app_api` keeps by column grant (OLC-02). It never named a residency column, so the trigger of CRF-04 does not fire for it. |
| CRF-10 [7I] | **Compatibility with the India-enterprise rules.** INV-14, Matrix 10, EGR-01 … EGR-12, AB-7I-06 and AB-7I-07 are unchanged. They read the profile; this section makes the profile trustworthy. The egress policy store and its platform-side guarded change function (EGR-03; IR-27) are a different object and keep their own rule: the residency profile is not editable through them. |
| CRF-11 [OD-7I-22, condition 12; OD-7I-25, condition 12] | **Audit evidence.** The creation function writes, in its one transaction: the consumed authorization with its references and both human identities; a provenance row (the STP-11 form: organization, pair, cause `PROVISIONING`, authorization reference, conformance-record reference, `session_user`, time); the frozen `ORGANIZATION_CREATED` audit row; and an audit row with the proposed action kind `RESIDENCY_PROFILE_ASSIGNED`, both visible in the organization's own audit trail. A refused creation writes nothing and raises. |
| CRF-13 [OD-7I-25, conditions 2, 3, 4, 16] | **The creation transaction is the frozen one, with the profile set.** The function performs, in one transaction, the statements of 6C §7.7 in their frozen order: insert the organization with `status = 'ACTIVE'` **and the pair (`INDIA_ENTERPRISE`, `in-primary`)**; set the transaction-local tenant context to the new identifier; insert the owner membership (`OWNER` role, `ACTIVE`); insert the `organization.created` row in `audit.domain_event_outbox` with the frozen event type, version and payload shape (EV-002); write the audit and provenance rows of CRF-11; consume the authorization. The compliance policy is **not** written here: it is seeded asynchronously by the Compliance consumer when the event is delivered, exactly as 6C §7.7 freezes it (CON-02), through its guarded seed function. No event name, payload field, route or state is added. |
| CRF-14 [OD-7I-25, conditions 6, 13, 14] | **There is no partially provisioned organization.** Before the commit no row of the organization is visible to any other session: no request can authenticate into it, because no membership is visible; no consumer can process for it, because its only event is an uncommitted outbox row that the relay cannot claim; no endpoint, callback input, object or delivery can exist for an identifier nobody outside the transaction knows. At the commit the organization, its owner membership, its creation event, its profile and its audit evidence become visible together. The first read of the organization by any consumer, including the compliance seed, sees `INDIA_ENTERPRISE`. A failure at any statement rolls back all of it and leaves nothing: no `ACTIVE` organization, no membership, no event, and the authorization still unconsumed for a retry. Platform-held dependencies that are not rows (the region's stores, keys and egress path) are properties of the conformant deployment and are established before the change runs (CRF-06 c); an organization-specific key that is created on first use fails closed if absent (INV-16). |
| CRF-15 [7I] | **Why the fourth review's interleavings cannot occur.** Each requires an organization that exists and accepts writes while its profile is still to be decided. No such organization exists: a `STANDARD` organization's profile is never decided again, and an enterprise organization's is fixed in the transaction that creates it. The seven cases are worked in §28.7. |
| CRF-12 [7I] | **What is not claimed.** The migration authority and a database superuser can write these columns, as they can write anything; that authority is outside every runtime boundary of this document and is controlled by the governed change process, not by a database rule. Whether an `INDIA_ENTERPRISE` assignment is correct in contract is the provisioning record's matter; the database verifies deployment conformance and the absence of data, not the contract. |

**The counterexamples, closed.** *Downgrade (third review).* With IR-46 applied, under `app_api`, `app_worker`, any context principal or `app_platform_admin`, with any session setting: `UPDATE organization.organizations SET data_residency_profile = 'STANDARD', region_ref = 'standard' WHERE id = …` fails with `42501`, because no login role holds `UPDATE` on either column; an `INSERT` that names either column fails with `42501`; and if a later migration mistakenly granted the column, or added a definer function, the trigger of CRF-04 would still raise for every caller. The egress adapter continues to read `INDIA_ENTERPRISE` and to refuse. *Provisioning race (fourth review).* A governed change that tries to make an existing `STANDARD` organization `INDIA_ENTERPRISE` has no function to call and its direct `UPDATE` is refused by the trigger even under the migration authority, so the step "provisioning commits the profile based on an earlier empty check" does not exist. A new enterprise organization is created with its profile in one transaction, before which nothing can be written for it. Until IR-46 exists the downgrade statement succeeds and no enterprise organization can be created correctly; AB-7I-12 therefore forbids creating or representing any organization as `INDIA_ENTERPRISE`, and AB-7I-06 continues to block `INDIA_ENTERPRISE` egress. Tests: VT-101, VT-102, VT-115, VT-116.

### 8.12 Organization integration erasure authority (P1-7I-R12; OD-7I-20)

Nothing in this section exists. It is a requirement on a future governed migration (IR-47) with a controlled erratum to 5I, 6J and this document's own OD-7I-17 closure (ERR-7I-18).

**The counterexample, on the executed schema.** A holder of the `app_platform_admin` login runs `SELECT integrations.fn_integrations_anonymize_org('<any organization>')`. `061_5I` L178 grants the role `EXECUTE`. The function is `SECURITY DEFINER`, owned by the migration role, which is `BYPASSRLS`, so the tenant policy on `integration_connections` does not apply inside it. Its body (L166 – L176) is one `UPDATE … WHERE organization_id = p_organization_id` that sets `external_account_name = '[redacted]'`, `external_account_ref = NULL`, moves every non-terminal connection to `DISCONNECTED` with `disconnected_at = NOW()`, and sets `disconnect_reason = 'gdpr_erasure'`. It checks nothing: not `is_platform_admin()`, not a tenant context, not an erasure request, not the organization's status, not a hold. It writes no audit row. `trg_ic_terminal_guard` then makes the disconnection permanent. A live tenant's integrations are severed and their account references destroyed on the strength of a UUID.

**A correction to the previous text.** ADM-06 said that "the 6M caller supplies" the audit write and the break-glass check. No such caller exists: 6M does not mention this function, defines no erasure route, and none of the six break-glass purposes of `105_5B4` is an erasure purpose. 6J §11 and §31 describe the function as "GDPR-erasure-only, platform-admin-gated" and "`app_platform_admin`/break-glass-only", which is a statement of intent with no enforcing mechanism. 5I §23 says the PII is "anonymized on org deletion". No frozen route or workflow invokes the function at all. The earlier sentence presented an undesigned control as existing and is withdrawn (F-7I-26).

**Which operation needs it, and who starts it.** One: organization erasure (ERA-17), when an organization that has been cancelled under the frozen lifecycle has its data removed. `external_account_name` is the name of the organization's own connected account (class `PII`, `061_5I` L29). The function is organization-wide; it is not a step of any data-subject request. Tenant disconnection is a different function, `integrations.fn_disconnect_integration_connection` (`101_5I1`; 6J §11), which does not anonymize.

**SQL privilege matrix, before and after.**

| Object | `PUBLIC` | `app_api` | `app_worker` | `app_platform_admin` | Event-operations tooling principal | Maintenance principal |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `integrations.fn_integrations_anonymize_org(UUID)` — today (`061_5I` L177 – L178) | Revoked | — | — | **`EXECUTE`** | (does not exist) | (does not exist) |
| The same — after IR-47 | None | None | None | **None** | None | None. The function stays, unedited, with an empty ACL; nothing calls it |
| Request, approve and withdraw functions of the erasure operation (new) | None | None | None | None | `EXECUTE`, with a `session_user` check | None |
| Execute function of the integration step (new) | None | None | None | None | None | `EXECUTE`, with a `session_user` check |
| The erasure-operation relation, its approval records and the consumed-proof relation (new) | None | None | None | None | None | None |
| `integrations.integration_connections` | — | `SELECT` (`061_5I` L49) | `SELECT` | All four today → none (ADM-01) | None | None |
| `integrations.fn_disconnect_integration_connection` and the other 6J connection functions (`101_5I1`) | Revoked | `EXECUTE`, unchanged | As today | Revoked (ADM-05) | None | None |

All new functions are `SECURITY DEFINER`, owned by the migration role, with a fixed `search_path` (PRV-16), `REVOKE ALL … FROM PUBLIC` (PRV-20) and a complete restated ACL (PRV-28).

**The authoritative erasure operation: state and binding.**

| Element | Definition |
|---|---|
| Record | One **organization-erasure operation** per erasure of one organization. Fields: operation identifier (database-generated); `organization_id`; purpose, the constant `ORGANIZATION_ERASURE`; **approved scope**, a set drawn from a closed vocabulary of stores, of which `INTEGRATION_CONNECTIONS` is the one this section executes; reason code and ticket reference (OPA-06); **plan fingerprint**, a digest over organization, purpose, scope, reason and ticket; requester identity and proof; approver identity and proof; approval expiry; state; times |
| States | `REQUESTED → APPROVED → EXECUTING → COMPLETED`; `REQUESTED → REJECTED`; `REQUESTED or APPROVED → WITHDRAWN`; `APPROVED → EXPIRED`. `COMPLETED`, `REJECTED`, `WITHDRAWN` and `EXPIRED` are terminal. **The only states in which a step may run are `APPROVED` and `EXECUTING`, and only while the approval is unexpired** |
| Bound to | Exactly one organization, fixed at request and immutable; the purpose; the scope; the requester and the approver as human identities; the plan fingerprint |
| Who writes it | Only the functions of OEA-04 … OEA-07. No login role has a table privilege on it |
| Per-store execution | Each scoped store is one erasure step (ERA-05) referencing the operation, with the journal states of JRN-06 |

| ID | Rule |
|---|---|
| OEA-01 [OD-7I-20, conditions 6, 7] | **The direct grant is removed.** `REVOKE EXECUTE ON FUNCTION integrations.fn_integrations_anonymize_org(UUID) FROM app_platform_admin`, and from `PUBLIC`; no role is granted it. A bare organization UUID together with an administrator database credential authorizes nothing. This withdraws the exception that ADM-06 and INV-21 had kept. |
| OEA-02 [OD-7I-20, condition 1] | **`CANCELLED` only.** An erasure operation is created, approved and executed only for an organization whose committed `status` is `CANCELLED`, read under a share lock on the organization row in each of the three functions. `CANCELLED` is terminal and writable by no direct statement (§8.10), so the status the function reads was produced by an authorized cancellation and cannot afterwards change. An `ACTIVE` or `SUSPENDED` organization's integrations cannot be anonymized by any path. |
| OEA-03 [OD-7I-20, conditions 3, 4] | **Hard dual control.** Requester and approver are different authenticated humans, compared on the human identity as in OPA-07: one person with two roles or two sessions cannot approve their own request. Two capabilities are added to §13.2, `erasure.organization.request` and `erasure.organization.approve`, granted under OPA-04 and never to oneself. There is no emergency self-approval and no single-operator path in V1. |
| OEA-04 [OD-7I-20, condition 5] | **Database-verifiable requests and approvals.** Each of the request and the approval carries an **operator action proof**: a keyed digest under the platform action key (OLC-07) over the purpose label (`ORG_ERASURE_REQUEST` or `ORG_ERASURE_APPROVE`), a unique proof identifier, the operator's user and session identifiers, `organization_id`, the scope, the plan fingerprint and, for the approval, the operation identifier, with an expiry. It is minted by the platform authorization issuer for an operator authenticated with fresh MFA (OPA-03). The request and approve functions verify the code with `pgcrypto`, require every bound field to equal the stored or supplied value, require the bound session to be `ACTIVE` in `identity.sessions`, require a live capability grant, and consume the proof identifier under a unique constraint in the same transaction. The verified proofs are stored on the operation. This is OPA-09 made verifiable inside the database, which is what condition 5 requires. |
| OEA-05 [OD-7I-20, conditions 8, 9] | **Separated executor.** The execute function is executable only by the maintenance principal (PRV-08) and checks `session_user`. Its **only argument is the operation identifier**. The maintenance principal holds no `EXECUTE` on the request, approve or withdraw functions, holds no key, and has no table privilege, so it can neither create nor approve an operation nor write a row that looks approved. The tooling principal, which can call request and approve, cannot compute a proof and cannot execute. `app_platform_admin` can do none of the three. |
| OEA-06 [OD-7I-20, conditions 2, 10] | **Verification at the mutation boundary.** In one transaction the execute function: locks the operation row; requires state `APPROVED` or `EXECUTING` and an unexpired approval; **re-verifies both stored proofs** under the key relation and re-compares the two human identities; re-checks both capability grants (OPA-10); takes the organization from the record, never from an argument; share-locks the organization row and requires `CANCELLED`; requires `INTEGRATION_CONNECTIONS` in the approved scope; takes the organization's hold gate in share mode (HLD-10) and evaluates the effective hold state of HLD-11 for the whole organization, treating as blocking any unreleased registry hold of that organization of either kind and any data-subject request of it in `ON_HOLD`; requires the step's intent to be durable in the independent journal (INV-23; JRN-06). Only then does it run the frozen statement of `061_5I` L169 – L174 for that organization, unchanged. No session setting and no caller-supplied organization, actor or flag is consulted (PRV-18). |
| OEA-07 [OD-7I-20, condition 12] | **Atomic audit.** The same transaction writes: the step's `ERASED` state with its counts (connections redacted; connections disconnected); the operation's state change; and an audit row through `audit.fn_insert_audit_event` with the proposed action kind `ORGANIZATION_INTEGRATIONS_ANONYMIZED`, carrying the operation identifier, the requester and approver identifiers, the scope and the counts, and no account name or reference. If the audit insert fails the mutation rolls back (AUD-7I-01; INV-13). The journal completion follows under JRN-06. Request, approval, rejection, withdrawal and expiry are audited in their own transactions (`ORGANIZATION_ERASURE_REQUESTED`, `_APPROVED`, `_REJECTED`, `_WITHDRAWN`, `_EXPIRED`); every refusal is audited under OPA-14. |
| OEA-08 [OD-7I-20, condition 11] | **Replay, duplication, substitution, expiry.** *Replay and reuse:* an operation names one organization for its whole life; a `COMPLETED`, `REJECTED`, `WITHDRAWN` or `EXPIRED` operation executes nothing; a proof identifier is consumed once; an approval is unique per (operation, plan fingerprint, approver) (OPA-13). *Duplicate execution:* the step moves to `ERASED` once under the operation's row lock; a second call finds it and reports "already erased" with nothing changed. *Cross-tenant substitution:* the organization is in the record and in both proofs; an operation or approval of organization A cannot act on B, and a proof for another operation fails on the bound operation identifier and fingerprint. *Expiry:* an approval lasts 24 hours (OPA-11) and is checked when the step's intent is requested and again at the mutation; an expired one moves the operation to `EXPIRED`. A plan edit changes the fingerprint and voids the approval (OPA-08). |
| OEA-09 [7I] | **Revocation.** If either operator's capability is revoked before the step commits, the execute function refuses (OEA-06) and the operation waits for a fresh approval. A session revoked before its request or approval call makes that call fail (OEA-04). A withdrawal by a holder of the request capability, with a proof, moves `REQUESTED` or `APPROVED` to `WITHDRAWN`. A hold placed before the mutation commits prevents it; one placed after finds the erasure done (HLD-03, HLD-04). An erasure that has committed is not reversible, and is not claimed to be. |
| OEA-10 [OD-7I-20, condition 13] | **Crash recovery and concurrency.** The step follows JRN-06 … JRN-09: no erasure without a durable intent, no completion without a database `ERASED`. A crash before the mutation commits leaves the operation `APPROVED` or `EXECUTING` with an intent; the maintenance principal resumes it while the approval is valid; after expiry the intent is withdrawn (JRN-08) and a new approval is needed. A crash after the commit and before the journal completion is recovered by JRN-09. Two concurrent executions serialize on the operation row. Two operations for one organization may both be approved; the first erases, the second finds the step's work already done and completes with zero counts. The statement itself is idempotent in its effect on `external_account_name`, `external_account_ref` and `status`. Nothing is lost by waiting: an erasure is not an event obligation. |
| OEA-11 [OD-7I-20, condition 13] | **The frozen erasure outcome is preserved.** After an authorized execution the organization's connections are exactly as `061_5I` leaves them: name redacted, reference cleared, non-terminal connections `DISCONNECTED` with reason `gdpr_erasure`. No column, value or state of 5I changes. Credential references (`credential_ref`) and their secret-manager entries are not touched by this statement, as today; their purge is 6J §42's and ERA-22's. |
| OEA-12 [FROZEN] | **Tenant integration management is unaffected.** `app_api` keeps `SELECT` on `integration_connections` and `EXECUTE` on the 6J connection functions (create, activate, fail, degrade, disconnect, update configuration, rotate, OAuth), each tenant-context guarded since `101_5I1` (ADM-09). None of them is called by, calls, or shares an ACL with the erasure functions. A tenant's own disconnect (6J §11) works on an `ACTIVE` organization exactly as before and does not anonymize. No tenant route and no platform-administrator route is added. |
| OEA-13 [OD-7I-20, condition 14] | **Subject-level erasure is separate and not restricted by this section.** A data-subject request for a contact of an `ACTIVE` organization proceeds through the erasure steps of §14.3 and §14.4 under its own authority (6C §13). It never calls the organization-wide function and is not subject to the `CANCELLED` precondition. Should a later owner context define a subject-level step for a person named in an integration's account name, that is a separately authorized, row-scoped Integrations step; nothing here forbids it and nothing here designs it. |
| OEA-14 [7I] | **Relation to ERA-17.** The erasure operation is the authority for organization erasure as a whole: ERA-17's removal of bodies, previews, processing inputs, material and keys for a cancelled organization runs as further scoped steps of the same operation, each through its own guarded function and its own gate (AB-7I-05). This section fixes the operation's authority and executes one store. |
| OEA-15 [OD-7I-20] | **What is and is not claimed.** *Prevented:* anonymization by a stolen `app_platform_admin`, `app_api`, `app_worker`, tooling or maintenance credential, alone or in any combination that lacks the issuer's key; anonymization of a live organization; execution on one approver; reuse of an approval. *Not prevented, and not claimed:* two colluding authorized operators acting on a cancelled organization (the T-7I-07 residual); a compromised platform authorization issuer or a reader of the key relation, which can mint both proofs (RR-09). The independence of the two humans rests on the issuer; RR-04 applies. |
| OEA-16 [7I; OD-7I-13, OD-7I-16] | **Restore safety.** The integration step is an irreversible privacy erasure and is journaled like every other (INV-23). Its journal record carries, as lifecycle evidence (JRN-22), the organization's `CANCELLED` status and cancellation time and the operation identifier. A database recovered to a point before the erasure, or before the cancellation itself, is quarantined (INV-18); the restore reconciler re-applies the step through a restore-only function, granted to it alone and refusing on an activated database (the JRN-25 pattern), which first brings the organization row to its journaled `CANCELLED` status and then runs the same anonymizing statement. The organization is taken from the journal record. This is the one path other than the lifecycle functions that moves a status, it moves it only to `CANCELLED`, only during quarantine, and it passes the transition trigger like any other (OLC-04). A restored organization is therefore never served as live with its erased integrations, and never with them un-erased. |

**The counterexample, closed.** With IR-47 applied, a holder of the `app_platform_admin` password runs the call above: PostgreSQL checks the function ACL before executing; the role is not in it, is a member of no role, and `PUBLIC` holds nothing; the result is `42501 permission denied for function fn_integrations_anonymize_org` and no row is locked. It cannot call the execute function (`42501`; and the body would raise on `session_user`). Suppose the attacker also holds the tooling and the maintenance passwords. To reach the mutation it needs an `APPROVED` operation, which only the request and approve functions can produce, each of which demands a code computed with a key that no login role can read, for two different human identities with live sessions and capability grants. It cannot write the operation row directly: no role has a table privilege on it. It cannot reuse an old approval: the operation is bound to its organization and is terminal once used. It cannot target a live organization: the function reads `CANCELLED` under lock. A legitimate erasure still completes: two operators request and approve, the maintenance job executes, and the mutation, its audit row and its step evidence commit together. Until IR-47 exists the original call succeeds; AB-7I-01 names it and AB-7I-05 blocks organization erasure. Tests: VT-103 … VT-106.

### 8.13 Tenant authorization root (P1-7I-R14; OD-7I-23)

Nothing in this section exists. It is a requirement on a future governed migration (IR-48) with a controlled erratum to 5B, 5I and 6M (ERR-7I-21).

**The counterexample, on the executed schema.** The attacker holds the `app_platform_admin` login and an ordinary, legitimately registered user account U. After IR-39 it cannot update a victim tenant's endpoint. It runs `INSERT INTO organization.memberships (organization_id, user_id, role_id, status, accepted_at) VALUES (<victim>, <U>, <system OWNER or ADMIN role id>, 'ACTIVE', now())`. The statement succeeds: `008_5B` L31 grants the role `SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE` on the table and the role is `BYPASSRLS` (`001_5B`), so the forced tenant policy of `003_5B` does not apply. `uq_memberships_active` is satisfied because U had no active membership there. U then logs in through the normal API. `organization.get_user_organization_ids` (`003_5B` L207 – L218) lists every organization in which U has an `ACTIVE` membership, so the victim is offered at organization selection (6B §9.3) and the access token carries its `organization_id` and the forged `membership_id` (6B §11.1). On each request 6B §8 evaluates exactly four things: the membership is `ACTIVE`, the organization is `ACTIVE`, the permission is in the role's set, else deny. All of it is read from the rows the attacker wrote. `webhook:manage` is granted, the tenant `PATCH` of `target_url` succeeds with a correct audit row and revision, and the next delivery carries the tenant's payload to the attacker. **Every step is permitted by the physical schema and the frozen authorization rule.** IR-39 closed the direct path and left this one.

**Three further routes to the same result were found by reading the same grants.**

| Route | Statement under `app_platform_admin` | Why it works today |
|---|---|---|
| Role promotion | `UPDATE organization.memberships SET role_id = <OWNER> WHERE user_id = <U>` | `008_5B` L31; no trigger constrains `role_id` |
| Permission widening for every tenant | `INSERT INTO organization.role_permissions` for a **system** role (for example adding `webhook:manage` to `VIEWER`), or `UPDATE organization.roles` | `008_5B` L34, L36. The tenant-side policy excludes system roles (`003_5B` L201 – L203) but does not bind a `BYPASSRLS` role; `protect_system_roles` guards only the name and the flag |
| Account takeover of an existing OWNER | `INSERT INTO identity.password_reset_tokens` with a token hash the attacker knows, or `INSERT INTO identity.oauth_identities` linking the attacker's own provider subject to the victim's `user_id` | `008_5B` L27, L28. `109_5B7` Part F revoked `identity.users`, `sessions` and `api_keys` (L1185 – L1187) and states that the role's "only remaining paths to identity data" are three views and one function; it left these two relations fully writable. Neither has RLS |

**What the platform administrator legitimately needs here.** Nothing. The 42 routes of the frozen 6M inventory (6M §25) were read one by one. None reads or writes any of the ten relations below: organization support reads `organization.organizations`; user, session and API-key support read the three safe views; the one identity command is `fn_platform_revoke_all_sessions`. 6M contains no reference to memberships, roles, role permissions, the permission catalogue, teams, data-subject requests, reset tokens or OAuth identities. Support access to a tenant is break-glass (6B §9.2, §18.3), which sets a tenant context for an authenticated platform-administrator session and does not use a membership.

**Authorization-root privilege matrix, before and after IR-48.** The "ten relations" are exactly the fourteen of `008_5B` L25 – L38 less the four that later migrations already narrowed.

| Relation | Authorization significance | RLS | `app_platform_admin` today (source) | Frozen 6M use | `app_platform_admin` after | `app_api`, `app_worker` (tenant path) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `organization.memberships` | Step 1 of 6B §8; the role reference; organization selection at login | Forced, tenant policy | All four (`008_5B` L31) | None | **None** | `SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE` (`003_5B` L137), unchanged |
| `organization.roles` | The role a membership points to; system roles have no organization | Forced; read admits system roles | All four (`008_5B` L34) | None | **None** | `SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE` (`003_5B` L92), unchanged |
| `organization.role_permissions` | Step 3 of 6B §8: the permission set | Forced; modify excludes system roles | All four (`008_5B` L36) | None | **None** | `SELECT, INSERT, DELETE` (`003_5B` L204), unchanged |
| `organization.permissions` | The global catalogue of permission strings | None | All four (`008_5B` L35) | None | **None** | `SELECT` (`003_5B` L108), unchanged. Written only by seed migrations (`007_5B`, `096_5B2`, `104_5B3`) |
| `organization.teams`, `organization.team_memberships` | Tenant structure; no V1 permission is derived from a team | Forced | All four (`008_5B` L32, L33) | None | **None** | `SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE` (`003_5B` L160, L182), unchanged |
| `organization.compliance_policies` | Tenant compliance configuration; `status` is a guard column (STP-01) | Forced | All four (`008_5B` L37); `UPDATE` and `DELETE` already withdrawn in design by STP-02 | None | **None** | As STP-02 leaves them |

| *Already narrowed:* `identity.users`, `identity.sessions`, `identity.api_keys` | Credentials, sessions, API keys and their scope ceiling | `api_keys` only | None on the tables; `SELECT` on three column-restricted views that omit every hash and secret reference (`109_5B7` L1044 – L1066, L1185 – L1187) | Three read routes; one command | Unchanged | Unchanged |

| Function reachable by the role | Today | Reads or writes authorization state? | After |
|---|---|---|---|
| `organization.get_user_organization_ids(UUID)` | `EXECUTE` (`003_5B` L218); definer | Reads memberships across tenants | **Revoked** from the role; `app_api`, `app_worker` keep it. No 6M route calls it |
| `identity.fn_platform_revoke_all_sessions` | `EXECUTE` (`109_5B7` L1178) | Sets sessions to `REVOKED` only; cannot create a session or a credential | Unchanged (6M route) |
