**FLD-28 [7I] — Disposition of the EV-078 hold.** The hold is closed as **NOT RELEASED**. `summary_text` is class `SEN`. It is never embedded in EV-078 or in any other event; it never appears in a webhook, a plugin payload, a log, a trace, a metric, an analytics projection fed by events, or replay material. The V1 payload stays as frozen: `conversation_id` only. CON-04 obtains the text in process through the Voice owner port under the event's tenant context and writes its CRM note (6G §23.1). Tenant-facing reads of the summary follow the frozen Phase-6 authorization unchanged; 7I neither widens nor narrows it. One observation is passed to 7L without action here: 6D returns `summary_text` under `call:read` while 6L gates transcript content with `transcript:access_content` (HE-7L-7I-05).

**The Class-F marks of 7B §16** (RTM-17 … RTM-20 transcript text, RTM-31 slot values) are WebSocket messages, outside the durable and SIGNAL paths. They are class `SEN`, governed by the realtime contract and its authorization (6A §27.4); no event, stream entry or webhook may be built from them (7B Rule F-1). Their channel-level authorization is not a 7I design and is unchanged.

### 10.3a EV-097 financial admission (OD-7I-14; P1-7I-R04)

**What the frozen sources say.** They do not agree, and 7I rewrites none of them.

| Source | Statement | Reading |
|---|---|---|
| 4D §4.6, §17.10 | `TotalCost` is "sum of telephony + AI costs"; `CostLookupPort.get_campaign_cost()` returns "sum of telephony + LLM + STT/TTS for all calls" | Does not say whose cost |
| 4F §2, §11 | A cost entry is "what the platform paid a provider … not the customer's price"; `GetCostBreakdown` is the implementation of `CostLookupPort` | **Provider procurement cost** |
| 4G §7.2 | ROI "Total Cost = SUM(`cost_entries.amount`)" | **Provider procurement cost** |
| 6L §26.2; DEC-6L-02 = A | The campaign cost and ROI figures in Analytics are provider-cost-sourced and are platform-internal; tenants may see ROI "based on their authoritative billed spend" | Provider cost must not reach a tenant; a billed basis may |
| 6H §26.1, §26.2 | `GET /campaigns/{id}/outcome` returns `total_cost` and `roi_pct` under `campaign:read`, described as "authoritative billed usage (Billing-owned output)"; until 6K implements the port both are `NULL` (ADR-6H-08; DEP-6H-13, still open) | **Customer-billed**, by intent |
| 7B §24; 7C EV-097 | `total_cost`: money, REQUIRED, **NULLABLE** ("`null` as a whole when not computed"); `roi_pct`: REQUIRED, **NULLABLE** | Both may be `null` in a valid V1 event |

**Determination.** The field's meaning is not settled by its name. Option A (provider procurement cost) is what the only described implementation of the port would return; option B (the customer's billed spend) is what 6H and DEC-6L-02 require a tenant-visible figure to be. Because A is possible, the earlier treatment of the field as harmless "because no consumer is bound" was wrong: the value is written to the outbox row, held there for at least 7 days, copied to the `LS-D-CPN` family stream where every reader of that family receives it, and included in every backup, whether or not any handler uses it.

| ID | Rule |
|---|---|
| FIN-01 [OD] | `total_cost` MAY contain only the customer's authoritative billed campaign spend. `roi_pct` MAY contain only a value computed from that billed spend and from revenue inputs the governing contracts permit (the tenant's configured `estimated_conversion_value`, 6H §26.2). |
| FIN-02 [OD] | Provider procurement cost, wholesale cost, platform margin and provider / customer spread never enter either field, as an amount or inside a ratio. |
| FIN-03 [OD] | Where a billed-spend basis or valid ROI inputs are unavailable, the field is `null`. It is never estimated, defaulted, fabricated or filled from provider cost. `null` is valid under the frozen 7C binding for both fields, so no schema change and no blocked emission is needed for the `null` case. |
| FIN-04 [OD] | **Basis attestation.** The cost port's result carries, with the amount and currency, a server-set **basis** from a closed set: `CUSTOMER_BILLED` or `PROVIDER_COST`. The Campaign producer has no other way to learn the basis and never infers it from the currency, the magnitude or the caller. A result without a basis is treated as `PROVIDER_COST`. |
| FIN-05 [OD] | **Enforced before publication.** In the outcome-computation transaction, before the outbox insert: if the basis is not `CUSTOMER_BILLED`, the producer writes `NULL` cost and `NULL` ROI to the outcome row and `null` to both event fields. Producer validation rule **PV-7I-01** rejects, by rolling the transaction back, an EV-097 payload whose `total_cost` or `roi_pct` is non-null while the transaction's recorded basis is anything other than `CUSTOMER_BILLED`. The check is on the producing side of the outbox; it does not rely on a tenant-facing serializer. |
| FIN-06 [OD] | **The row and the event agree.** The 7C binding takes both event fields from the outcome row. The gate therefore applies to the row first: a provider-basis amount is never stored in `campaign.campaign_outcomes`. This also keeps the 6H tenant read consistent with DEC-6L-02, which is that owner's contract and is recorded, not changed (CNF-7I-12). |
| FIN-07 [OD] | **Confidential regardless of consumers.** EV-097 is classified by its content. The absence of a bound consumer lowers nothing. Analytics' platform-internal provider-cost projections (`campaign_outcome_summary` cost columns, `roi_by_campaign`) are never fed from EV-097; they read Billing under `analytics_platform:read` as 6L defines. |
| FIN-08 [OD] | **Server-authoritative.** Cost and ROI are computed by the platform from Billing-owned and Campaign-owned state. No tenant input, request field or event field supplies or overrides either (6H §26.2 unchanged). |
| FIN-09 [OD] | **No provider-cost field is added** to any event, and no platform-internal economics are published to a general-purpose stream. A future consumer that needs provider cost obtains it from Billing by identifier under platform-internal authorization. |

**Activation gate (AB-7I-09).** Until a `CostLookupPort` implementation exists that returns the `CUSTOMER_BILLED` basis from Billing's customer-charge data, EV-097 is emitted with `total_cost = null` and `roi_pct = null`, which is today's frozen behaviour (ADR-6H-08). Emission of a non-null value is blocked until the port, PV-7I-01 and VT-69 exist. The controlled erratum for the upstream wording is ERR-7I-11.
### 10.4 Minimization and schema evolution

| ID | Rule |
|---|---|
| MIN-01 [7I] | A `PII` or `SEN` field that a frozen V1 binding already carries stays, because removing a field is BREAKING under 7C §29 and 7I may not change a schema. It is controlled by encryption of copies, the logging prohibition and erasure. |
| MIN-02 [7I] | Six `SEN` free-text fields (FLD-09, 10, 17, 21, 30, 31) and four `PII` fields with no current consumer (FLD-03, 04, 27, 29) are recorded as **minimization candidates**: a future governed 7C version should replace each with a reference. This is a recommendation to 7L (HE-7L-7I-03), not a change made here. |
| MIN-03 [7I] | Name-list fields carry names from a closed vocabulary. A producer never places a tenant-defined label, a value or free text in them. Producer validation enforces the vocabulary (IR-20). |
| MIN-04 [7I] | The five unbound marks are **not approved** for V1. Binding any of them is 7C MX-16 and needs a new 7I review and, for `PII` / `SEN`, an owner decision. `target_url` is never to be bound. |
| EVO-01 [FROZEN] | A new sensitive or personal field is never COMPATIBLE because it is optional (7C SP-04). It is `PROHIBITED_UNTIL_SECURITY_OR_OWNER_REVIEW`. |
| EVO-02 [7I] | **Review rule for MX-16.** A proposed field is admitted only with: a classification; a named consumer that cannot obtain it by identifier; its logging, external, encryption and erasure treatment in the form of §10.3; and, for `PII` or `SEN`, an owner decision. `SEC`, `FIN-P`, transcript, utterance, recording and presigned-URL content are never admitted. |
| EVO-03 [7I] | Widening an existing field (a code that becomes free text, an identifier list that becomes labels) is a new field for this purpose. |
| EVO-04 [7I] | An upcaster never adds a field of class `PID` or higher (7C UPC-12 extended to `PID`). |
| EVO-05 [7I] | A change to a field's class in the manifest is a governed change with the same review. Lowering a class needs an owner decision. |
| EVO-06 [7I] | **Envelope metadata.** Field-level class of the frozen envelope: `event_id`, `correlation_id`, `causation_id` — `PID` when the event is about a person (they join to it), otherwise `TEN`; `event_type`, `event_version`, `durability` — `OPS`; `organization_id` — `TEN`; `aggregate_type` — `OPS`; `aggregate_id` — the class of what it identifies (`PID` for contact, call, conversation, appointment); `occurred_at` — `PID` with the aggregate. None is secret. All may travel and be stored as case identity; none is a metric label (RED-07). |
| EVO-07 [7I] | **Trusted routing metadata versus payload values.** Routing, scope and identity decisions use envelope fields only. No component routes, scopes, authorizes, deduplicates or selects a tenant from a payload value (7C PAY-05; INV-02). |

### 10.5 Validation failures and unknown versions

| Situation | Security behaviour | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Producer validation fails | Transaction rolls back; the error names type, version, field path and rule ID; **never a value** | 7C PV-04, PV-08 |
| Consumer finds a malformed entry | No side effect; exact bytes parked as encrypted material; the observation carries a category code and no content | 7C CV-08; 7G RPM-06; RED-03 |
| Unknown `event_version` of a known type | No guess, no nearest version, no partial apply; held then parked; signal names type, version, consumer, stream; no value | 7C UV-01 … UV-05 |
| Unknown `event_type` | No side effect; compatibility hold | 7C UV-07; 7G FC-06 |
| Payload organization differs from the envelope | Contract-invalid; parked; a tenant-scope signal is raised | 7F TEN-7F-02; HE-7J-7I-05 |
| An error path wants to include "the offending value" | Prohibited. The path and rule ID identify the defect; the bytes are in material for an authorized view | RED-04 |

### 10.6 Redaction rules

One rule set, applied at named boundaries. "Never" means the value is not emitted; it does not mean it is emitted and later filtered.

| ID | Surface | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| RED-01 | Application and structured logs | Carry: event identity, type, version, safe category codes, counts, durations, workload identity, and identifiers of class `TEN` and `PID` on internal restricted sinks. Never carry a payload, a body, material, a processing input, a header value, a URL beyond scheme-host-port, or any field of class `PII`, `SEN`, `SEC`, `FIN-P`. Payload logging is off and no production configuration enables it (7D SEC-7D-02). |
| RED-02 | Transport components | The relay, publishers, trim worker and provisioning never log `env` (7E SCY-03). |
| RED-03 | Failure and observation metadata | A closed category code (7G FCL-07; 7H HTP-14) and bounded numeric facts. No error text with data, no database message with values, no exception string. |
| RED-04 | Exception reports | An exception that could hold a value is caught at the boundary and replaced by its category; local variables and request bodies are not attached to error reports for event-pipeline code. |
| RED-05 | Traces | Span attributes are drawn from an allow-list: identity, type, version, category, counts, durations. No payload, body or `PII`+ attribute. The destination is scheme, host and port (7H LOG-7H-02). |
| RED-06 | Organization scope in internal logs (7D HO-7I-01) | The organization UUID, or the literal `platform`, in internal operational logs and traces only. Never in a metric label, never in a log another tenant can read, never in an unrestricted support export. A case with an untrusted scope is logged as `untrusted`, never as an organization. |
| RED-07 | Metric labels | Closed, low-cardinality sets only: group, family, event type, category, origin, mode. Never an organization, user, contact, call, event, delivery or case identifier; never a host name; never a free value. |
| RED-08 | Redis diagnostics | `XINFO` and `XPENDING` output (class `INT`) may be recorded. Output of `XRANGE` or `XREADGROUP` is never recorded. `MONITOR` is denied (RDS-10). |
| RED-09 | DLQ and recovery tooling | The default view is the redacted view of §13.5. Material is never exported to a ticket, a log, a file or a clipboard helper (7G AUT-07). |
| RED-10 | Audit attributes | `resource_snapshot` is non-personal and non-secret by construction (5J §14.1). 7I audit rows carry identifiers, capability names, counts, reason references and category codes. They carry no payload, material, URL, path, query, fingerprint input or free-text justification that could hold tenant data (the justification is a ticket reference). |
| RED-11 | Platform-admin dashboards | Delivery metadata only: no `payload_json`, no response preview (IR-09). Recovery cases are not shown on the 6M surface at all. |
| RED-12 | Tenant dashboards and APIs | The frozen DTOs of 6J §23 and 6L §34, plus the failure origin of OD-7I-08 (§11.5). Never a worker identity, a hash, a secret role, an egress rule code, a pinned address, a history record or a recovery case. |

### 10.7 Receiver-response previews (7H HE-7I-7H-06)

The stored preview is at most 512 characters of content from a server the tenant chose but the platform does not trust.

| ID | Rule |
|---|---|
| PVW-01 [7I] | The preview is built at the recording boundary, before it is stored, in this order: decode as UTF-8 with replacement of invalid sequences; remove every C0 and C1 control character, including NUL, CR, LF, TAB and escape; remove bidirectional-override and zero-width characters; apply secret masking (PVW-03) and personal-data masking (PVW-04); truncate to 512 characters. |
| PVW-02 [7I] | It is stored and returned as plain text inside a JSON string. No surface renders it as HTML, Markdown, a link or terminal output. A user interface displays it as escaped text. |
| PVW-03 [7I] | **Embedded secrets.** Masked with a fixed token before storage: anything after `Authorization:` or `Bearer`; three-part base64url tokens; `secret_manager://` references; `key=`, `token=`, `password=`, `secret=`, `signature=` values; long opaque runs of base64 or hexadecimal characters (32 or more); the platform's own signature header values. A receiver that echoes the request would otherwise store the platform's signature. |
| PVW-04 [7I] | **Echoed personal data.** E.164 numbers and email addresses are masked. The preview is nonetheless classified `PII`-possible: masking is pattern-based and a receiver may echo a name. It is therefore erased together with the body in every erasure of §14 and §15. |
| PVW-05 [7I] | The preview is never parsed, never used to decide retry behaviour beyond the status code, never forwarded and never logged. |
| PVW-06 [7I] | A redirect's `Location` value is never stored (7H DST-09). |
| PVW-07 [7I] | The same rules apply to the bounded previews of `plugin_executions` (7H PLG-12). |
| PVW-08 [7I] | The preview column is withdrawn from the platform-admin read path with the body (IR-09). |

## 11. External Payload Security

### 11.1 Rules

| ID | Rule |
|---|---|
| XPL-01 [FROZEN] | `data.object` is built by a per-topic allow-list serializer. It is never a row dump and never the internal payload forwarded (6J §40.1; 7H PRJ-01). |
| XPL-02 [OD-7H-07] | The 7H V1 baseline (7H §5.3) is preserved exactly. 7I **does not narrow it and does not widen it**. Every field in it is either an identifier, a timestamp, a code, an amount a frozen contract names, or a contact field 6J §40.2 names for that topic. |
| XPL-03 [7I] | A `PII` field is in a body only for the four topics 6J §40.2 names (`lead.created`, `lead.qualified`, `appointment.booked`; email for the two `lead.*` topics). No `SEN`, `SEC`, `INT` or `FIN-P` field is in any body. |
| XPL-04 [7I] | A serializer is tested against Matrix 4: its key set equals the allowed set, and a fixture that injects every excluded field proves none can appear (7H IO-7H-01, extended to the classes of §10.1). |
| XPL-05 [7I] | **History records on tenant surfaces.** Claim, admission, abandonment and closure records are not exposed to tenants. The tenant sees the delivery DTO of 6J §23 plus the failure origin (§11.5). |
| XPL-06 [7I] | A port-read field (7H PRJ-03) is read under the event's tenant context and reflects state at fan-out. A contact erased before fan-out therefore yields `null` contact fields, never the erased values (7H PRJ-04). |

Classes of the fields 7H §5.3 allows. "Body class" is the highest class in the body and decides its erasure treatment.

**No compatibility conflict.** The baseline is left exactly as 7H froze it, so no governed erratum to a public projection is raised. Three topics carry direct personal data to a destination the tenant configured; that is the stated purpose of those topics in 6J §40.2 and is the reason §15 and §18.4 exist.

### 11.3 Never in any external body

Raw transcript text; recording content; full utterances; signed or presigned media URLs; access or refresh tokens; API keys; provider secrets; raw provider payloads; payment credentials; GSTIN and address snapshots; provider procurement cost; gross margin; free-text CRM details (reasons, notes, deal titles); internal identifiers of the delivery machinery (`webhook_endpoint_id`, `attempt_count`, `claimed_by`, `payload_hash`); any class `INT` value. Source: 7H PRJ-06; 6J §20.2, §39, §40; 6K §45.1; 6L DEC-6L-02; §10.2.

### 11.4 The three external boundaries stay separate

| Boundary | Direction | Signing identity | Credential namespace | Canonical input | Never shared with |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Public webhook | Out, to a tenant endpoint | The endpoint's signing secret | `webhook_endpoints.signing_secret_ref` | `ts={X-Platform-Timestamp}.{raw_request_body}` | Plugin callouts; provider adapters |
| Plugin callout | Out, to a plugin service | The installation's secret | `plugin_installations.credential_ref` | `ts={unix_timestamp}.{method}.{canonical_request_path}.{raw_body}` | Webhooks; provider adapters |
| Provider callback | In, from a provider | The provider's own scheme, verified with the connection's or the platform's provider credential | Integration and provider credential references | Provider-defined, over the raw bytes | Both of the above |

**XPL-07 [FROZEN].** No builder, secret, key or verification routine of one boundary is used for another (7A WH-10; 7H SIG-03, SEC-7H-02). The resolver of each credential namespace is a different workload identity at the secret manager: dispatcher for webhook secrets, executor for plugin secrets, provider adapters for integration credentials.

### 11.5 Tenant-visible failure detail (OD-7I-08; closes HE-7I-7H-10)

| ID | Rule |
|---|---|
| TVF-01 [OD] | A tenant sees, for a failed or dead-lettered delivery, the sanitized `failure_reason` **category code** from the frozen closed list of 7H HTP-14 and its **origin**: `RECEIVER`, `DESTINATION`, `PLATFORM` or `TENANT_CONFIGURATION`. The vocabulary and its classification are 7H's, unchanged. |
| TVF-02 [OD] | A tenant never sees: which signing-secret role (CURRENT or PREVIOUS) could not be resolved; any secret reference; secret-manager state; worker identity; the internal egress rule code; a pinned or blocked address; an internal host name; a stack trace; a configuration value; a claim sequence, admission or abandonment record. |
| TVF-03 [7I] | The origin is carried in the tenant DTO as a derived, read-only value next to `failure_reason`. It adds no route, no public error code and no new state. Whether it is serialized as a separate key or as part of the existing field is an additive response detail under AVS CM rules, recorded as API follow-up APF-02 (§21.4). Until that is consolidated, the category code alone is shown; each code maps to exactly one origin, so nothing is lost. |
| TVF-04 [7I] | Authorization and tenant isolation of every delivery read are unchanged: `webhook:read`, RLS, `404` across tenants. |
| TVF-05 [7I] | Detailed diagnostics (secret role, rule code, pinned address, lock waits) exist only on restricted internal observability surfaces (HE-7J-7I-03). |
| TVF-06 [OD-7I-02] | Abandonment records (AB) follow their delivery's metadata retention like every other history record (RET-05). |

## 12. Encryption and Key Management

No vendor is named. The frozen deployment architecture has not selected a secret manager or a key service (ASM-02). The design is stated against two abstract ports: a **key service** that wraps, unwraps and computes keyed digests without exporting root keys, and the **secret manager** already assumed by 3F.

### 12.1 Key hierarchy

```
Regional root key            (in the key service of that region; never exported)
  └─ Organization key-encryption key, one per (organization, purpose)      [KEK]
       └─ Record data key, one per stored record, wrapped by the KEK       [DEK]

Platform key-encryption key, one per (region, purpose)   -- records with no trusted organization
Destination-evidence key, one per region, versioned      -- keyed digest only (7H DST-02)
```

Purposes are closed: `REPLAY_MATERIAL`, `CALLBACK_INPUT`, and, on the platform key only, `ERASURE_JOURNAL` (JRN-04). A key of one purpose never decrypts a record of another.

| ID | Rule |
|---|---|
| KEY-01 [7I] | **Envelope encryption.** A record is encrypted with a fresh 256-bit data key under an authenticated cipher (AES-256-GCM or an equivalent AEAD). The data key is wrapped by the organization's KEK for that purpose and stored beside the ciphertext. |
| KEY-02 [7I] | **Associated data.** The AEAD associated data binds the ciphertext to its row: purpose, organization (or the literal `platform`), the owning record's identifier, and the schema version. A ciphertext moved to another row, organization or purpose fails authentication. |
| KEY-03 [7I] | **Stored metadata.** Each record stores: algorithm identifier, KEK reference and KEK version, wrapped data key, nonce, ciphertext, and the SHA-256 of the plaintext that 7G RPM-02 and 7H MR-7H-09 already require. No key material is stored in clear. |
| KEY-04 [7I] | **Tenant isolation.** One KEK per organization per purpose. Compromise of one KEK exposes one organization's records of one purpose. Records without a trusted organization (EV-001 material, `CONSUMER_UNIDENTIFIED` and `TRANSPORT_INTEGRITY` cases) use the platform KEK of that purpose. |
| KEY-05 [7I] | **Environment and region isolation.** Root keys are per region and per environment. A non-production environment cannot unwrap a production key. An `INDIA_ENTERPRISE` organization's keys exist only in its contracted region (RSY-08). |
| KEY-06 [7I] | **Encrypt without decrypt.** A consumer worker that parks an entry needs to encrypt and never to decrypt. Its workload identity holds only "generate a wrapped data key" on `REPLAY_MATERIAL`. It receives the data key once, uses it and discards it; it cannot unwrap a stored one. Decrypt on `REPLAY_MATERIAL` is held by exactly two workloads: the replay executor and the material-view service. |
| KEY-07 [7I] | The material-view service decrypts in memory and returns the redacted view by default. Unmasked output requires the live grant of §13.5; the service checks it against the database on every request (OPA-14). |
| KEY-08 [7I] | For `CALLBACK_INPUT`: the ingress workload (API) holds generate-only; the callback-processing workload holds decrypt. No other workload, and no operator, holds either. |
| KEY-09 [7I] | **Rotation.** A new KEK version is used for records written from then on. Older versions become decrypt-only. No bulk re-encryption is required, because most records age out within the 90-day and 7-day limits. **A version is not retired because a standard retention window has elapsed.** A recorded hold (§14.7), an operation that still references material (ERA-15), an open erasure step or a restorable backup can each keep a record, or a need to read one, alive past those windows. Retirement is KEY-19. |
| KEY-10 [7I] | **Recovery during rotation.** A record names the KEK version that wrapped it. A replay or a callback recovery that starts under version n and finishes after n+1 is active still reads version n. Rotation never invalidates a stored record. |
| KEY-11 [7I] | **Compromise.** A suspected KEK compromise: disable new use; rotate; identify the records wrapped by that version from the stored KEK reference; treat their content as disclosed for incident handling; the records themselves stay readable for recovery. A suspected data-key compromise affects one record. |
| KEY-12 [7I] | **Destination-evidence key** (7H MR-7H-10; closes HE-7I-7H-09). Custody: the key service, as a keyed-digest key that is not exportable where the service supports that; otherwise the secret manager with read access for two workloads only. **Calculate:** the endpoint-mutating API workload, at creation and at every `target_url` change. **Compare / verify a candidate URL:** an investigation function in event-operations tooling, under the capability `evidence.destination.verify` (§13.2), with a ticket and an audit row per verification. **Never:** the dispatcher, any consumer, any tenant surface. |
| KEY-13 [7I] | The dispatcher copies the stored fingerprint and key version from the endpoint row into the admission record. It never computes one, so it never needs the key (7H DST-03, DST-06). |
| KEY-14 [7I] | **Evidence-key rotation.** A new version applies to revisions created afterwards (7H DST-10). Correlation is by revision, never by comparing digests made under different versions. Old versions are kept verify-only while any history record, audit row, held record or restorable backup references them. Audit rows are retained far longer than deliveries (5J §20), so an old version is destroyed only through KEY-19, when the audit rows that cite it have left retention, or earlier by an explicit, recorded, dual-controlled decision that those rows' fingerprints become unverifiable. |
| KEY-15 [7I] | **Evidence-key compromise.** The digest is a privacy boundary, not an integrity control. With the key, a guessed URL can be tested offline against stored fingerprints. Response: rotate; restrict the old version to verify-only under dual control; record which revisions it covers. No delivery behaviour changes. |
| KEY-16 [7I] | **Access logging.** Every key-service operation is logged by the key service with workload identity, purpose, organization and operation, never a key or a plaintext. Decrypt on `REPLAY_MATERIAL` outside an operation item or a live view grant is an alert (HE-7J-7I-07). |
| KEY-17 [7I] | No key, wrapped key, secret value, secret reference or fingerprint input appears in any event payload, stream entry, metric, log or trace (INV-07). |
| KEY-18 [7I] | **Erasure.** Three different things, never treated as one: **record deletion** removes one record's ciphertext and wrapped data key from the primary store, and the record is then unrecoverable there; **key destruction** renders every remaining ciphertext under that key version unreadable wherever it is, backups included (cryptographic erasure); **backup expiry** is the only thing that removes a copy from backup media. Record-level erasure does **not** make backup copies unreadable; §14.8 keeps them inaccessible through any restored service. Erasing an organization's data additionally destroys its KEKs, through KEY-19, after the retention of §14 has run and no hold applies. |
| KEY-19 [7I] | **Governed key retirement** (Minor-7I-R02). A KEK version, an organization's KEK or an evidence-key version is destroyed only when all of the following are established and recorded: (a) an **authoritative reference count of zero**, taken by a guarded database function over every relation that stores a key reference for that purpose (material, processing inputs, captured sources; history and audit rows for the evidence key), not inferred from elapsed time; (b) **no active hold** links to any record that was wrapped by the version (HLD-08); (c) **backup reconciliation**: either no restorable backup contains a record wrapped by the version, or the destruction is itself the intended cryptographic erasure of those copies and is recorded as such; (d) the key service's backup or recovery set will not resurrect the version, or the resurrection is covered by the journal (JRN-02 `KEY_DESTROYED`); (e) a **destruction decision** under dual control by holders of `retention.hold.manage`, with a ticket and an audit row. Until then the version stays decrypt-only (or verify-only). |
| KEY-20 [7I] | **Recovery guarantees kept.** KEY-10 is unchanged: a referenced version is always readable, so a replay, a callback recovery or a held record never fails because of rotation. A destruction that would strand a referenced record is refused by (a). A destruction is journaled before it is executed (JRN-06 applies to keys as to rows), so a restored key-service state cannot bring a destroyed version back into use unnoticed. |

### 12.2 Failure of a key or secret dependency (fail closed, obligation preserved)

| Operation | Dependency unavailable | Outcome | Obligation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Parking an entry | Cannot obtain a data key | Parking transaction is not attempted; no `XACK` | Entry stays pending (7G RPM-05, PAT-03) |
| Callback receipt | Cannot obtain a data key | Receipt is not committed; the route answers 5xx | The provider retries; nothing was acknowledged |
| Replay of a case | Cannot unwrap | The item is not started; the operation pauses (7G THR-05 pattern) | Case stays `PARKED` |
| Callback processing | Cannot unwrap | Processing claim is released; the receipt stays for the sweep | Receipt stays owed |
| Material view | Cannot unwrap or cannot verify the grant | No output | — |
| Webhook send | Signing secret unresolvable | `SECRET_UNAVAILABLE`, `NOT_SENT` (7H OD-7H-13, OD-7H-17) | Delivery follows the frozen schedule |
| Endpoint creation or URL change | Evidence key unavailable | The mutation is refused | Nothing changed |

In no row is plaintext stored, a request sent unsigned, or a check skipped (INV-16).

### 12.3 Matrix 8 — Sensitive-data storage and encryption

| Store | Content | Highest class | In transit | At rest | Field-level encryption | Who can read plaintext | Erasure mechanism |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `audit.domain_event_outbox.payload` | Event payloads | `SEN` | TLS | Storage-level | No (frozen `JSONB`; the relay reads it) | The relay principal, through the claim function, for rows that call claimed (target state; today also `app_worker` and `app_platform_admin`, F-7I-14) | Frozen 7 / 30-day cleanup under the interlocks of 7G and ACC-06; guarded payload tombstone for an undispositioned `FAILED` row (ERA-07) |
| Redis durable and SIGNAL streams | Envelopes | `SEN` | TLS | Storage-level persistence volume | No (RDS-04) | The stream gateway, which forwards each entry to the registered consumer of its group | Safe trim only; never per entry |
| Recovery ledger — case, observation, history, operations | Identity, state, counters, references | `PID` | TLS | Storage-level | No | Tooling role through functions | 90 days after resolution (7G PRT-01) |

| STO-01 [FROZEN] | Object keys are tenant-prefixed and built by the owning context's storage port from the trusted organization (5A §19). |

This is a precondition recorded for 7L, not a V1 mechanism. |

## 13. Replay / DLQ Operator Authorization

The capabilities and the state machine are 7G's and are not changed. 7G AUT-03 left to 7I: who holds each capability, whether separation is hard, and how it is enforced.

### 13.1 Rules

| ID | Rule |
|---|---|
| OPA-01 [FROZEN] | Recovery, replay, redrive, backfill and group operations exist only as internal event-operations tooling. There is no tenant-facing route and no Phase-6 route (7G AUT-01). |
| OPA-02 [OD-7I-05, OD-7I-07] | **No capability is implied by a role outside this section.** A tenant `OWNER` or `ADMIN`, an API key, a normal worker and a holder of the `platform_admin` claim hold none of them. The platform-admin claim is neither necessary for, nor sufficient for, any recovery capability. |
| OPA-03 [7I] | **Operator identity.** An operator is an authenticated human user of the platform's own identity system with MFA enrolled and verified for the session. An action that approves, executes, dispositions or requests unmasked material additionally requires an MFA verification no older than a short bound ([REC] 15 minutes). No frozen step-up mechanism exists (6B §13); this is a requirement on the internal tooling's authentication, not a public API change. |
| OPA-04 [7I] | **Capability grants** are durable records in the ledger's schema: operator, capability, scope (region; optionally target groups), granting identity, granted and expiry times, revocation. A grant is made by an identity holding `recovery.capability.administer`, never to itself, and is audited. The first grants are seeded by a governed, owner-approved change. A grant expires; [REC] 90 days. |
| OPA-05 [7I] | **System identities** hold capabilities by the same records, scoped to what their function needs: the owning domain's reconciliation path holds `recovery.reconciliation.record` for its own groups only; the maintenance principal holds `recovery.maintenance.cleanup`; the day-83 job holds no disposition capability (OPA-17). |
| OPA-06 [7I] | **Reason and ticket** (closes HE-7I-7G-04). Every operation carries: a reason code from a closed list; a ticket reference in the configured tracker's format, which the tooling validates for existence and open state at request time; and, for a disposition, the proof category or the owner reference 7G §24.4 requires. Free text with tenant data is not accepted in any of these (7G §18.1). |
| OPA-07 [OD-7I-05] | **Hard dual control.** For R3 backfill, R4 disaster replay, R5 publisher redrive, group retirement, `XGROUP SETID` repair and every operation whose target is a high-risk group (CON-06 Billing, CON-10 Integrations; 7G §41.1), the approver MUST be a different authenticated human from the requester. The comparison is on the **human identity**, not the session, the role or the credential: one person with two roles or two sessions cannot approve their own request. There is no emergency self-approval in V1. |
| OPA-08 [OD-7I-05] | **Approvals are bound to the plan.** An approval names the operation ID and the fingerprint of the immutable plan: mode, source, target groups, candidate set, reason, ticket, dry-run result and plan version. Execution proceeds only while the stored fingerprint equals the approved one (7G PLN-05). Any edit creates a new plan version and voids the approval. |
| OPA-09 [7I] | **Evidence of the approver.** The approval record stores an assertion issued for that approver and that plan fingerprint by the central internal token issuer (6B §17), so the approval can be verified independently of the tooling process that recorded it. This is the compensating control for RR-04. |
| OPA-10 [OD-7I-05] | **Re-validation.** Capability, scope, grant validity and MFA freshness are checked when the request is made, when it is approved, when execution starts and at every batch boundary. A stale, revoked, expired, modified or mismatched approval is refused. |
| OPA-11 [7I] | **Approval lifetime.** An approved plan that has not started within 24 hours expires and needs a new approval. The Redis credentials of the repair publisher and the recovery operator are retrievable by the tooling workload only while an approved operation of the matching kind is `RUNNING`. |
| OPA-12 [7I] | **Revocation during an operation.** If the requester's or approver's capability is revoked, or the grant expires, the operation moves to `PAUSED` at the next item boundary. Items already `REPLAYING` are completed by the operation's recovery so that each case reaches a definite state (7G CAN-03). Resuming needs a fresh approval. Nothing is rolled back and nothing is cancelled silently. |
| OPA-13 [7I] | **Idempotent decisions.** An approval is unique per (operation, plan fingerprint, approver). Re-submitting it returns the stored decision. A refusal is likewise stored and returned. |
| OPA-14 [7I] | **Audit on refusal.** Every refused request, approval, execution, disposition or view writes an audit row with outcome `FAILURE` and a category. If that audit write fails, the action remains refused and an alert is raised; a refusal never turns into a permission. |
| OPA-15 [FROZEN] | **No generic discard of a valid obligation.** `PERMANENTLY_REJECTED_WITH_REASON` is unavailable for a class `V` case to every actor, enforced in the ledger (7G DAU-02, MR-18). 7I binds principals to capabilities and cannot widen which transitions exist (7G DAU-06). |
| OPA-16 [7I] | **No alternate path.** Ad-hoc SQL against the ledger or the outbox and ad-hoc Redis commands against stream keys are not available to any operator identity: the tooling role has no table privilege (PRV-09), operators have no database or Redis credential, and administrative break-glass to either store is an infrastructure identity whose use is alerted and is never a recovery procedure (7G AUT-06; RDS-11). |
| OPA-17 [OD-7I-11] | **A scheduler is not an authority.** The day-83 job runs validation and records the result. It holds no `recovery.case.disposition` and changes no case state except by routing a now-valid case to the R2 process as a candidate. |
| OPA-18 [7I] | **Roster.** High-risk recovery needs two authorized people. The operating organization maintains an on-call roster with at least two holders of the relevant request capability and two holders of `recovery.replay.approve` reachable for incident recovery. This is an operational precondition recorded as AB-7I-03 (c); waiting for the second person loses nothing, because parked obligations are durable. |

### 13.2 Capabilities

The twelve capabilities of 7G §40 are unchanged. 7I adds six for functions that 7G did not define.

| Capability | Permits | Origin |
|---|---|---|
| `recovery.case.read` … `recovery.maintenance.cleanup` (twelve) | As 7G §40 | 7G |
| `recovery.material.view.approve` | Approving one unmasked view of one case's material | 7I (OD-7I-07) |
| `recovery.capability.administer` | Granting and revoking capability grants, never to oneself | 7I |
| `evidence.destination.verify` | Testing a candidate URL against a stored destination fingerprint | 7I (7H DST-11) |
| `retention.hold.manage` | Placing and releasing a platform-recorded hold on event-pipeline copies (§14.7) | 7I |
| `erasure.organization.request` | Requesting, and withdrawing, an organization-erasure operation for a `CANCELLED` organization (§8.12) | 7I (OD-7I-20) |
| `erasure.organization.approve` | Approving or rejecting one such operation, never one's own request | 7I (OD-7I-20) |

### 13.4 Authorization is consistent across retry and recovery

| Path | Authorization evaluated | When |
|---|---|---|
| Normal consumer attempt | Envelope scope; owner guards | Every delivery |
| Sweep redelivery | Same | Every delivery; nothing is cached from an earlier attempt (TCX-06) |
| R2 item | Operation approval (OPA-10); then the same consumer pipeline | At start and each batch; then per item |
| Webhook attempt | Organization status; endpoint revision; egress policy | Every admission and every request (7H ADM-01, ELK-01; EGR-05) |
| Public replay | `webhook:manage`; organization and endpoint status; lineage window and quotas; body present | In the replay transaction |
| Callback recovery | Tenant from the receipt; owner guards | Every processing attempt |

### 13.5 Material view (OD-7I-07)

| ID | Rule |
|---|---|
| MAT-01 [OD] | **Default view is redacted.** It shows: the envelope structure; field names; types; the schema version; which validation step failed and its rule ID; for each value of class `PID` or higher, a mask and its length class. `OPS`, `TEN` identifiers and enum codes are shown. For bytes that cannot be parsed (CLS-04) it shows length, digest and the parser's failure position, and no bytes. |
| MAT-02 [OD] | **Unmasked view** needs all of: `recovery.material.view` held by the requester; an approval by a different human holding `recovery.material.view.approve`; a ticket specific to that case; a stated purpose from a closed list; an expiry. |
| MAT-03 [OD] | The approval is bound to **one** recovery case, to the requester's identity (immutable) and to a validity of at most 60 minutes. It is not transferable and not renewable; a further view needs a new approval. |
| MAT-04 [OD] | Authorization is re-validated on **each** unmasked access: grant live, capability live, MFA fresh, case unchanged in identity. |
| MAT-05 [OD] | **Audit before release.** The access audit row commits before any unmasked byte leaves the service. If the audit write fails there is no output. Denials and expiries are audited too. |
| MAT-06 [OD-7I-07; 6M DEC-6M-03] | For a case with a trusted organization, each unmasked access also writes a tenant-scoped audit row visible to that organization: that a platform operator accessed event diagnostic data for a stated purpose category, with the time and no case detail. This applies 6M's "no hidden support actions" rule. It reveals nothing about the recovery ledger's content. |
| MAT-07 [OD] | Unmasked material is rendered in the tooling session only. It is never written to a log, a ticket, a trace, an export, an error response, a support dashboard or a file, and the tooling offers no download. |
| MAT-08 [OD] | Enforcement is at the service and at the key service, not in the user interface: the decrypting service returns masked output unless it has verified the grant against the database; the key service permits decrypt on `REPLAY_MATERIAL` only to that service and to the replay executor. |
| MAT-09 [OD] | **Fail closed.** If the approval, the capability record, the audit path or the decrypt authority is unavailable, the answer is no output. |
| MAT-10 [OD] | Revocation of the grant, of either capability or of the case's material (erasure) ends access immediately; the next access fails MAT-04. |
| MAT-11 [FROZEN] | Reading case metadata never grants reading material (7G AUT-07). No tenant-facing surface exposes a case or its material (7G TEN-7G-07). |
| MAT-12 [7I] | The replay executor decrypts material only to feed it, unchanged, to the 7F pipeline for an approved item. It exposes no bytes to an operator. |

## 14. Retention and Data Subject Rights

### 14.1 Retention domains are separate

Each row has its own clock. None implies another. **A Redis time-to-live or trim is never legal or business retention** (7A §32.3).

| Domain | What it holds | Authority for its retention |
|---|---|---|
| Business data | Owner tables | Each owning context; `RetentionProfile` (4I §9.4) |
| Outbox | Publication obligations | `077_5J1`: `PUBLISHED` 7 days, `FAILED` 30 days under the 7G interlock |
| Redis Streams | Transport copies | 7E safe trim; no duration |
| Recovery-ledger metadata | Cases, observations, history, operations | OD-7G-03: 90 days after resolution; unresolved never ages out |
| Replay material | Exact entry bytes | OD-7I-09, OD-7I-10, OD-7I-06 (§14.5) |
| Webhook delivery metadata and history | Rows, hashes, claim / admission / abandonment / closure records | 6J §22.6: 30 / 90 days; OD-7I-02 for `CANCELLED` |
| Webhook bodies and previews | `payload_json`, `last_response_body_preview` | With the row, and earlier under OD-7I-01, OD-7I-02 (§15) |
| Callback processing inputs | Normalized verified facts | 7H OD-7H-08; OD-7I-03 (§16) |
| Audit | Accountability records | 5J §20: 1 year hot, 7 years cold |
| Recordings and transcripts | Media and text | Voice; `RetentionProfile`; not an event store |
| Object storage | Binary objects | Owning context; no event copy in V1 (STO-04) |
| Backups | Point-in-time copies of all PostgreSQL stores | Deployment (3F); value owned by 7K |
| Legal holds | Preservation instructions | §14.7 |
